The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He: ﴿All praise is due to God, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter. And He is the Wise, the All-Aware.﴾ (1)

Exalted is He, says: Perfect gratitude and complete praise belong entirely to the One worthy of worship, who is the owner of everything in the seven heavens and everything in the seven earths, apart from all that they worship and apart from everything else. No one owns any of that besides Him. The meaning of His being the owner of all of it is: ﴿and to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter﴾, that is, to Him belongs perfect gratitude in the Hereafter, just as it belongs to Him in the present world. This is because all blessings come from Him to everyone in the heavens and the earth in this world, and from Him they will come in the Hereafter. So praise belongs to God alone, exclusively, in the immediate world and in the deferred Hereafter, because all blessings come from Him, and no one other than Him shares in them. And He is the Wise in His management of His creation and His disposal of them according to His decree, the All-Aware of them and of what benefits them, of what they have done and what they will do, encompassing all of that.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And He is the Wise, the All-Aware﴾: Wise in His command, All-Aware of His creation.

* *

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He: ﴿He knows what enters into the earth and what emerges from it, and what descends from the heaven and what ascends into it. And He is the Merciful, the Forgiving.﴾ (2)

Exalted is He, says: He knows what enters the earth and what hides within it of anything. From their saying "walajtu fi kadhā" (I entered into such-and-such) when one enters it, as the poet said:

"I saw the rhymes entering as entrances, / constricted, so that the needles cannot pass through them."

By His words ﴿entering as entrances﴾ He means: entering their places. ﴿And what emerges from it﴾, says: and what comes out of the earth. ﴿And what descends from the heaven and what ascends into it﴾, meaning: and what ascends into the heaven. That is a report from God that He is the Knower, to whom nothing in the heavens and the earth is hidden, whether it is apparent in them or concealed. And He is the Merciful, the Forgiving: He is Merciful to the people of repentance among His servants, not punishing them after their repentance, and Forgiving of their sins when they repent from them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 2–3:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come to us." Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you — the Knower of the unseen. Not an atom's weight escapes Him in the heavens or on the earth, nor is there anything smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear register."﴾ (34:3)

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: "And those who disbelieve among your people, O Muhammad, who denied the power of Allah to restore His creation after their annihilation to the form they had before their annihilation, ask you to hasten the coming of the Hour, mocking your promise to them and denying your report. Say to them: 'Yes, it will come to you, by my Lord,' swearing by Him that the Hour will surely come to you." Then, after mentioning the Hour, He, may His majesty be exalted, returned to speak of Himself and to glorify it, saying ﴿the Knower of the unseen﴾.

The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of Medina read ﴿ʿĀlimu al-ghayb﴾ in the pattern of fāʿil, with a nominative ending, as a new resumptive clause (isti'nāf), since an intervening statement came between His saying ﴿wa-rabbī﴾ and His saying ﴿ʿĀlimi al-ghayb﴾. Some of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read ﴿ʿĀlimi﴾ in the pattern of fāʿil, but they put it in the genitive, treating it as a response to His saying ﴿wa-rabbī﴾, since it is one of its attributes. The rest of the majority of the reciters of Kufa read ﴿ʿAllāmi al-ghayb﴾ in the pattern of faʿʿāl, in the genitive, agreeing with the case of His saying ﴿wa-rabbī﴾, since it is one of its epithets.

The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is that all three of these readings are well-known readings among the reciters of the regions, and their meanings are close. Whichever of them the reciter reads is correct. However, the most preferable of these readings to me is that one recites ﴿ʿAllāmi al-ghayb﴾ according to the reading I mentioned from the majority of the reciters of the people of Kufa. As for choosing ʿAllām over ʿĀlim, it is because it is more emphatic in praise. As for the genitive in it, it is because it is an attribute of the Lord, and it is in the genitive position. By His saying ﴿ʿAllāmi al-ghayb﴾ He means the Knower of what is hidden from the sight of creatures so that no one sees it, whether what has not yet come to be but will come to be, or what has already come to be but He has not let anyone else know of it. In this place, He, may His praise be exalted, described Himself with knowledge of the unseen, informing His creation that no one other than Him knows the time of the Hour's coming, even though it is coming. So He said to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: "Say to those who disbelieve in their Lord: 'Yes, by my Lord and your Lord, the Hour will surely come to you.' But no one knows the time of its coming except the Knower of the unseen, from whom not an atom's weight escapes."

By His saying, may His praise be exalted, ﴿lā yaʿzubu ʿanhu﴾, He means: it is not hidden from Him, but is manifest to Him.

Those who held the view of interpretation said something similar to what we have said on this matter. [Those who said this are:]

⁕ Ali narrated to us, who said: Abu Salih narrated to us, who said: Muawiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿lā yaʿzubu ʿanhu﴾: He says: it is not hidden from Him.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, who said: Abu Asim narrated to us, who said: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, who said: al-Hasan narrated to us, who said: Warqa narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah: ﴿lā yaʿzubu ʿanhu﴾: he said: it is not hidden.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿lā yaʿzubu ʿanhu mithqālu dharrah﴾, i.e.: it is not hidden from Him.

We have already explained this with its evidences earlier, in a way that makes repeating it in this place unnecessary.

The commentary on His words, exalted is He: ﴿That He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds; those will have forgiveness and noble provision﴾ (4).

He, exalted is His mention, says: I have affirmed that in the Clear Book, so that He may reward those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, who act upon what Allah and His Messenger have commanded them, and who refrain from what He has forbidden them, out of their obedience to their Lord. ﴿Those will have forgiveness﴾ — He, whose praise is majestic, says: for these who believe and do righteous deeds there is forgiveness from their Lord for their sins. ﴿And noble provision﴾ — He says: and a pleasant life on the Day of Resurrection in Paradise.

As related:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Those will have forgiveness﴾: for their sins; ﴿and noble provision﴾: in Paradise.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who strive against Our verses, seeking to frustrate them, for them is a painful punishment of a terrible kind﴾ (34:5).

Our Lord, exalted is His remembrance, says: Establish that in the Book, so that He may recompense the believers with what He has described, and so that He may recompense those who strive against Our verses, seeking to frustrate them. He means: and so that He may reward those who labour to invalidate Our proofs and Our arguments, [[(In Lisan al-Arab, under ʿ-j-z): "Mu'ajizin" means they seek to outdo the prophets and the friends of God, that is, they fight them and resist them, so as to bring them to a state of incapacity (al-muʿjiz) regarding God's command. It is said: "So-and-so competes to make others incapable of the truth in favour of falsehood," meaning he inclines toward it and takes refuge in it.]] supposing that they can outrun Us by their own means, so that We will not be able to seize them. ﴿For them is a punishment﴾: He says, these people have a punishment from the severe punishment, the painful. Those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding God's saying ﴿And those who strive against Our verses, seeking to frustrate them﴾: "They strive, exerting themselves, to bring them down or to invalidate them." He said: "They are the polytheists," and he recited ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and talk noisily during it, that perhaps you may prevail﴾ (41:26).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 6:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth, and it guides to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: "He established that in a clear Book, so that He may recompense those who believed and those who strove against Our signs, [with] what has been made clear to them, and so that those who have been given knowledge may see." The word "yara" (may see) is in the accusative place, being coordinated by conjunction with His saying "yajziya" (may recompense) in His saying ﴿so that He may recompense those who believed﴾. By "those who have been given knowledge" he means the Muslims among the People of the Book, such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and his counterparts, who had read the Books of God that were revealed before the Furqan (the Criterion, i.e., the Qur'an). So He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: "And so that these who have been given knowledge of the Book of God, which is the Torah, may see that the Book which has been revealed to you, O Muhammad, from your Lord, is the truth."

It was said: By "those who have been given knowledge" is meant the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth﴾, he said: "The Companions of Muhammad."

* *

As for His saying ﴿and it guides to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾

He says: "It guides whoever follows it and acts upon what is in it to the way of God, the Mighty in His vengeance against His enemies, the Praiseworthy in His creation, so His bounties are with them and His favours are upon them." What is meant is that the Book which was revealed to Muhammad guides to Islam.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 7:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you that when you have been completely disintegrated, indeed you will be in a new creation?"﴾

Exalted is He, says: And those who disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) said, amazed at his promise to them of resurrection after death, to one another: ﴿Shall we direct you⁠—O people⁠—﴾ ﴿to a man who will inform you that when you have been completely disintegrated, indeed you will be in a new creation?﴾ That is, he will tell you that after you are scattered in the earth as decayed remains [[balaʾ (بلاء): with a fatha on the bāʾ and a long vowel, is a verbal noun of baliya (بلي), with a kasra on the lām. One says: baliya al-thawb, balan wa balaʾan (from Lisan al-Arab), meaning the garment wore out.]] and after your return to dust as crumbled bones, you will return in your former state before death, a new creation.

As related:

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you that when you have been completely disintegrated"﴾: He said, "That was said by the polytheists of Quraysh and the polytheists among mankind." ﴿Will inform you that when you have been completely disintegrated⁠—﴾ when the earth has consumed you and you have become crumbled remains and bones, and beasts of prey and birds have torn you apart ﴿indeed you will be in a new creation?⁠—﴾ you will be made alive and resurrected.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿Shall we direct you to a man…﴾ up to ﴿a new creation﴾: He said: "It means: ﴿when you have been completely disintegrated﴾, and when you have worn away and become bones, dust and crumbled remains, that is ﴿completely disintegrated, indeed you will be in a new creation﴾." He said: "He will inform you that you⁠—" so the inna is kasra and does not govern the verb yunabbi'ukum, but begins a new statement, because al-naba' (news) is both report and speech. So the kasra on inna is for the sense of narration in His saying ﴿yunabbi'ukum﴾, not its wording, as if it were said: He says to you, ﴿indeed you will be in a new creation﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 8:

The exposition of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Has he invented a lie against Allah, or is there madness in him?﴾ Nay, ﴿those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in punishment and far error.﴾ (8)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says, relating the saying of those who disbelieved in Him and denied resurrection after death, some of them saying to others, marveling at the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in his promise to them of that: "Does this one who promises us that, after we are torn apart in every tearing, we will be a new creation, invent a lie against Allah, fabricating by it false speech and inventing the utterance of falsehood against Him?" ﴿Or is there madness in him?﴾ That is, "Or is he insane, so that he speaks what has no meaning?"

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said the same as what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us from Qatadah, who said: They said, denying: ﴿Has he invented a lie against Allah?﴾ He said: They said: Either he lies against Allah, or he is a madman. ﴿Or is there madness in him?﴾ ﴿Nay, those who do not believe...﴾ the verse.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Then some of them said to others, ﴿Has he invented a lie against Allah, or is there madness in him?﴾ The man is mad, speaking what he does not understand. So Allah said: ﴿Those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in punishment and far error.﴾

And His words, ﴿Nay, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in punishment and far error.﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: The matter is not as these polytheists said about Muhammad (ﷺ) and supposed about him, that he invented a lie against Allah, or that there is madness in him. Rather, those of these polytheists who do not believe in the Hereafter are in the punishment of Allah in the Hereafter, and in going far astray from the path of truth and the right way; therefore, for this reason, they say about him what they say.

Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, Allah said: ﴿Nay, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in punishment and far error.﴾ And He commanded him to swear to them so that they would take heed, and he recited: ﴿Say: Yes, by my Lord, you will surely be resurrected, then you will surely be informed...﴾ the entire verse, and he recited: ﴿Say: Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you.﴾

The alif in His words ﴿Has he invented (aftara) against Allah﴾ is cut, both in pausal and continuous recitation, and it is given a fatha because it is the alif of interrogation (alif al-istifham, the interrogative alif). As for the alif that follows it, which is the alif of the form ifta'ala, it is dropped, because it is light and extra and falls away in connected speech. Its parallels are ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them﴾ (astaghfarta), and ﴿by My two hands, have you become proud﴾ (astakbarta), and ﴿has He chosen daughters﴾ (asta'fa, read with the alif of interrogation), and what is similar to that. As for the alif of ﴿Ālān﴾ and ﴿Ālladhdhakarayni﴾, these are lengthened, while those are not lengthened, because Ālān and Ālladhdhakarayn had a fatha, so if it were dropped there would be no difference between the interrogative and the declarative. So lengthening was made in them as a distinction between the interrogative and the declarative, and the interrogative alif carries a fatha, so the two were thereby distinguished, and the distinction by lengthening sufficed as an indication of difference.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Have they not looked at what is before them and what is behind them of the heaven and the earth? If We willed, We would cause the earth to swallow them, or cause a piece of the sky to fall upon them. Indeed in that is a sign for every servant who turns back in repentance.﴾ (34:9)

Our Lord, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Have these deniers of the Return, who reject resurrection after death and who say to Our Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿Has he invented a lie against Allah, or is there madness in him?﴾, not looked at what is before them and what is behind them of the heaven and the earth, so that they would know that wherever they are, My earth and My heaven encompass them, from before them, from behind them, from their right and from their left? Then they would refrain from their ignorance and desist from their denial of Our signs, fearing that We might command the earth to swallow them, or the sky to fall upon them in pieces, for indeed, if We willed to do that to them, We would do it.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Have they not looked at what is before them and what is behind them﴾, he said: They look to their right and to their left, how the sky has encompassed them. ﴿If We willed, We would cause the earth to swallow them﴾ as We swallowed those before them. ﴿Or cause a piece of the sky to fall upon them﴾, that is: pieces of the sky.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for every servant who turns back in repentance﴾

Our Lord, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed in the encompassing of the heaven and the earth around the servants of Allah is a sign, that is: a proof for every servant who turns back (anāba) to his Lord in repentance, and returns to knowing His oneness, acknowledging His lordship, confessing His unity, and submitting to His obedience, that the one who does this cannot be prevented from doing anything He wills to do, nor is anything He wishes to do beyond His reach.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿Indeed in that is a sign for every servant who turns back in repentance﴾, he said: The munib is the one who turns toward and repents.

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:** ﴿And We had certainly given David grace from Us. "O mountains, echo the praises with him, and the birds." And We made iron pliable for him﴾ (10). ﴿"Make coats of mail, and measure well the links, and work righteousness. Indeed, I am Seeing of what you do"﴾ (11).

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: We had given David grace from Us, and We said to the mountains, ﴿"Echo the praises with him"﴾, meaning: glorify (sabbih) with him when he glorifies. In the Arabic usage, *al-ta'wib* (returning, repeated echoing) means returning, and a man's spending the night in his dwelling and with his family. From this is the saying of the poet:

*Two days: a day of stays and gatherings, and a day of travel toward the enemies, returning (ta'wib).*

Abu 'Ubaydah cited it in *Majaz al-Qur'an* (the Jami'ah manuscript no. 26059, p. 197 b), and see it in *al-Mufaddaliyyat*, Cairo edition of 1926. *Al-ta'wib* is to spend the night with one's family. The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind; its morning [journey] was a month's [travel] and its evening [journey] was a month's [travel]. The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying ﴿wa-li-Sulaymana al-rīḥa﴾. The majority of the readers of the major cities recited ﴿al-rīḥa﴾ with a fatḥa on the rīḥ (al-rīḥa), meaning: "And We certainly gave David grace from Us... and We subjected the wind to Solomon." ʿĀṣim recited ﴿al-rīḥu﴾ with a ḍamma, in the nominative, by means of the preposition (ḥarf al-ṣifa), since the governing verb did not appear.

The correct recitation in this matter, in our view, is the fatḥa, because of the consensus of the authoritative readers upon it.

* *

As for His saying ﴿its morning [journey] was a month's [travel]﴾:

He, exalted is He, says: We subjected the wind to Solomon; its morning journey, until midday, was a month's travel, and its evening journey, from midday until night, was a month's travel.

The people of interpretation said in accordance with what we have said.

Those who said that:

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿And to Solomon the wind; its morning [journey] was a month's [travel] and its evening [journey] was a month's [travel]﴾: He said, "It travels a month's distance in the morning and a month's distance in the evening," and said, "a two-month distance in one day."

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us from Abu Ishaq, from some people of knowledge, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, concerning ﴿And to Solomon the wind; its morning [journey] was a month's [travel] and its evening [journey] was a month's [travel]﴾: He said, "It was mentioned to me that a dwelling in the region of the Tigris had written in it a letter written by one of Solomon's companions, whether from the jinn or from mankind: 'We descended upon it, and we did not build it; and [it is] a built [place] that we found. We set out in the morning from Istakhr and rested at midday, and we will depart from it, God willing, and spend the night in Syria.'"

- Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿And to Solomon the wind; its morning [journey] was a month's [travel] and its evening [journey] was a month's [travel]﴾: "He had a vessel of wood, and in it were a thousand pillars, and at each pillar a thousand chambers, in which the jinn and mankind would ride; beneath each pillar a thousand devils, who would lift that vessel, they and the whirlwind (al-ʿiṣṣār) [the whirlwind is what raises the dust, the ʿiṣṣār being a fierce dust storm]. When it rose, the wind came gently and carried it along, and they travelled with it. He would take his midday rest (yaqīlu) among a people at a distance of a month from them, and he would reach evening (yumsī) among a people at a distance of a month from them, and the people would not know until the armies and hosts had overshadowed them with him."

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abu ʿAmir related to us, saying: Qurrah related to us from al-Hasan, concerning His saying ﴿its morning [journey] was a month's [travel] and its evening [journey] was a month's [travel]﴾: He said, "He would set out in the morning and take his midday rest in Istakhr, then he would depart from it in the evening, and its evening [journey] would be at Kabul."

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Hammad related to us, saying: Qurrah related to us from al-Hasan, with the like of it.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And We caused a spring of molten copper to flow for him﴾:

He says: We melted for him a spring of brass (nuḥās), and We caused it to flow for him.

The people of interpretation said in accordance with what we have said.

Those who said that:

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us from Qatadah: "A spring of brass (ʿayn al-nuḥās) which was in the land of Yemen; and what God brought forth for Solomon is benefited from today."

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿And We caused a spring of molten copper to flow for him﴾: "Ṣifr (yellow brass) flowed as water flows; it was worked as dough is kneaded in milk."

- ʿAli related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Muʿawiyah related to me from ʿAli from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying ﴿And We caused a spring of molten copper to flow for him﴾: He said, "The brass (nuḥās)."

- Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying ﴿And We caused a spring of molten copper to flow for him﴾: He means: the spring of brass was made to flow.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And among the jinn were those who worked before him by the permission of his Lord﴾:

He, exalted is He, says: Among the jinn are those who obey him, carry out his command and desist at his prohibition; so they work before him what he commands them, in obedience to him, by the permission of their Lord, meaning: by God's command to that and His subjecting them to him. ﴿And whoever deviates from them from Our command﴾: meaning, whoever among the jinn slips and turns aside from Our command, which We commanded them, to obey Solomon. ﴿We will make him taste of the punishment of the Blaze﴾: in the Hereafter, and that is the punishment of the blazing Fire of Hell.

The people of interpretation said in accordance with what we have said.

Those who said that:

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us from Qatadah, and as for His saying ﴿And whoever deviates from them from Our command﴾: i.e., whoever among them turns aside from Our command, that which Solomon commanded him ﴿We will make him taste of the punishment of the Blaze﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 13:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They made for him whatever he willed of sanctuaries (maharib), statues (tamathil), basins like cisterns (jawab), and fixed cooking-pots. Work, O family of Dawud, in gratitude; and few of My servants are grateful.﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: The jinn make for Sulayman whatever he wills of maharib. Mihrab is the plural of mihrab, and the mihrab is the front of every mosque, house, and place of prayer. From it is the verse of 'Adi ibn Zayd:

Like the ivory ornaments in the maharib, or like the white ones in the meadow whose flowers shine forth. [[The verse belongs to 'Adi ibn Zayd al-'Ibadi, as the author said, and as in Shu'ara' al-Nasraniyya, fourth section, p. 455. The author cited it at (3 / 2464) of this tafsir, as evidence that maharib is the plural of mihrab, which is the front of the place of worship. Refer to it there.]]

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿whatever he willed of maharib﴾: He said: buildings below palaces.

- Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿They made for him whatever he willed of maharib﴾: and palaces and mosques.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿They made for him whatever he willed of maharib﴾: He said: the maharib are the dwellings. And he recited the saying of God ﴿Then the angels called to him while he was standing in prayer in the mihrab﴾.

- 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid al-Amali related to me, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiya told us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak regarding ﴿maharib﴾: He said: the maharib are the mosques.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and statues﴾:

He means that they make for him statues of brass and glass.

As:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding ﴿and statues﴾: He said: of brass.

- Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah regarding ﴿and statues﴾: He said: of glass and the like.

- 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid told us, saying: Marwan told us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak regarding the saying of God ﴿and statues﴾: He said: the images.

* *

His saying ﴿and basins like cisterns (jifan ka-al-jawab)﴾:

He says: they carve for him whatever he wills of basins like cisterns. Al-jawab is the plural of jabiya, and the jabiya is the basin into which water is collected, as the poet al-A'sha Maymun ibn Qays said:

A large bowl comes around at the assembly of al-Muhallaq, like the Iraqi old man's cistern, overflowing. [[The verse belongs to al-A'sha of Banu Qays ibn Tha'laba (his Diwan, Cairo edition, p. 225), and its transmission is: "Nafa al-dhamma 'an Al al-Muhallaq jafnatun ... ka-jabiyat al-sih al-'iraqi tafhaqu", a well-known variant like the one the author cited. It praises al-Muhallaq for generosity, saying that his bowl, full of meat and fat, circulates in his assembly; it is among the large bowls, like the water cistern in which the Iraqi old man collects water in the days when the river floods, to spend from it in the days of scarce water, so it is a large cistern. As for the one who narrated "al-sih" with sin and ha (unpointed), it is what overflows of water and flows out from the river's increase. Al-Mubarrad in al-Kamil mentioned both variants (see the Mustafa al-Babi al-Halabi edition, 1:7). He said in explaining the variant of the old man: thus the people of Basra recite it, and its interpretation among them is that the Iraqi, when he gains access to water, fills his cistern, because he is a townsman, so he does not know the places of water nor its seasons. Abu al-'Abbas said: I heard a Bedouin woman recite (she is Umm al-Haytham al-Kilabiyya, of the descendants of al-Muhallaq; and this is the variant of the people of Kufa): "kajabiyat al-Masih", meaning: the river flows along its two banks, so its water never ceases, because the river sustains it. End quote. Abu 'Ubayda said in Majaz al-Qur'an (folio 198), regarding "and basins like cisterns": its singular is jabiya, the basin into which water is collected. al-Farra' said in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (folio 261): "jifan" are large dishes, and "al-jawab" are the troughs for camels. In Lisan (j-b-y): al-jabiya is the basin in which water is collected for camels, and the jabiya is a huge basin, and he cited the verse in the author's variant, then said: he specified the Iraqi because of his ignorance of waters, being a townsman; if he finds them, he fills a cistern and prepares it, and does not know when he will find water.]]

As another said:

So I came upon a plastered cistern, its surface like the skin of the sky outside. [[These are two verses of rajaz (mashtur). Lisan (s-h-r-j) transmits the first from al-Azhari: "a cistern plastered with lime (al-nura); al-saharij and al-sahrij are alike." Al-Azhari recited: "fasabbahat jabiyatan sahariju..." The subject of "sabbaha" is a pronoun referring to what preceded, perhaps the camels. The rajaz is unattributed. His saying "kaannaha jild ..." (the verse) compares the color of the cistern or its water to the blue of the sky. This verse, like the one before it, is evidence that the meaning of jabiya is the large basin in which water is collected, and also sahraj and sahrij. He likened al-Muhallaq's bowl to a large basin, for his generosity.]]

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

- 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿and basins like cisterns﴾: He says: like the hollows of the earth.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿and basins like cisterns﴾: he means by al-jawab: the troughs.

- Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayya told us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan regarding ﴿and basins like cisterns﴾: He said: like troughs.

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying ﴿and basins like cisterns﴾: He said: troughs of camels.

- Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah regarding ﴿and basins like cisterns﴾: He said: basins like the hollows of the earth in size, the hollow of the earth being where water pools.

- It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿and basins like cisterns﴾: like troughs.

- 'Amr told us, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiya told us, saying: Juwaybir told us, from al-Dahhak regarding ﴿and basins like cisterns﴾: He said: like the camel troughs, of great size.

* *

His saying ﴿and fixed cooking-pots (qudur rasiyat)﴾:

He says: and cooking-pots that are firm, which are not moved from their places and do not shift because of their size.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying ﴿and fixed cooking-pots﴾: He said: huge.

- Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah regarding ﴿and fixed cooking-pots﴾: He said: huge, firmly fixed to the earth, not moving from their places.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying ﴿and fixed cooking-pots﴾: He said: like the mountains in their hugeness, food being prepared in them because of their size and bulk, not moved or transported, as He said of the mountains: fixed (rasiyat).

* *

His saying ﴿Work, O family of Dawud, in gratitude﴾:

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: And We said to them: Work in obedience to God, O family of Dawud, in gratitude to Him for the blessings upon you with which He has singled you out above the rest of His creation, along with gratitude to Him for the rest of His blessings which encompass you together with the rest of His creation. The phrase "And We said to them" is omitted, being sufficiently indicated by what the discourse implies of what was left out. He placed the word ﴿shukran﴾ as a verbal noun (masdar) from ﴿i'malu Al Dawud﴾, because the meaning of ﴿i'malu﴾ is: give thanks to your Lord by your obedience to Him, and working by what pleases God is thanks to God.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih told us, saying: Musa ibn 'Ubada told us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b regarding His saying ﴿Work, O family of Dawud, in gratitude﴾: He said: Gratitude is fear of God and working by His obedience.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Haywa informed me, from Zahra ibn Ma'bad, that he heard Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Hublí [[al-Hublí: with the ba' unpointed or pointed, a nisba to Banu al-Hublá, a clan of the Ansar, reliable; died in the year 100 (from al-Taj).]] say: ﴿Work, O family of Dawud, in gratitude﴾, and the best gratitude is praise.

He said: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: ﴿Work, O family of Dawud, in gratitude﴾: He gave you, taught you, and subjected to you what He did not subject to others, and taught you the speech of birds. Be grateful to Him, O family of Dawud. He said: praise is a part of gratitude.

* *

His saying ﴿and few of My servants are grateful﴾:

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: and few of My servants are those who are sincere in My unity, who single out My obedience and My gratitude for My blessings upon them.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

- 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying ﴿and few of My servants are grateful﴾: He says: few of My servants are those who affirm My oneness with their monotheism.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 14:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then when We decreed death for him, nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating away at his staff. So when he fell, the jinn saw clearly that, had they known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment.﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: When We carried out Our decree of death upon Solomon, and he died, ﴿nothing showed them his death﴾, meaning: nothing revealed to the jinn the death of Solomon, ﴿except a creature of the earth﴾, which is the termite (al-arda), that got into the staff on which he was leaning and ate it. This is the meaning of the saying of God, mighty and majestic: ﴿eating away at his staff﴾.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

- Ibn al-Muthanna and Ali told me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿except a creature of the earth eating away at his staff﴾: he said, the termite eats his staff.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd told us, saying: my father told me, saying: my uncle told me, saying: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿eating away at his staff﴾: he said, his staff.

- Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told me, saying: Isa told us, and al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿except a creature of the earth﴾: he said, the termite, ﴿eating away at his staff﴾: he said, his staff.

- Muhammad ibn Umara told me, saying: Abdullah ibn Musa told us, saying: Isra'il informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿eating away at his staff﴾: he said, his staff.

- Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Ibn Uthma told us, saying: Sa'id ibn Bashir told us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿eating away at his staff﴾: it ate his staff until he fell.

- Musa ibn Harun told us, saying: Amr told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "al-minsa'a" means the staff in the Abyssinian tongue.

- Yunus told us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "al-minsa'a" is the staff.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying ﴿minsa'atahu﴾. The majority of the readers of Medina and some of the readers of Basra recited it ﴿minsatahu﴾ without hamza. Those among the Basran readers who supported this reading argued that al-minsa' means the staff, and that its origin is from "nasa'tu bihi al-ghanam" (I drove the sheep with it). He said: it is from the hamzated forms which the Arabs have dropped, just as they dropped the hamza in "al-nabiyy", "al-bariyya" and "al-khabiyya". He cited for dropping the hamza in this word a verse by one of the poets:

When you grow old and lean on the staff from decrepitude, / Then idle talk and amorous dalliance have gone far from you.

Abu Ubayda's cited verse in Majaz al-Qur'an (the Folio 198b) has "habbaita" in place of "dabbabta"... [The source note on this verse is transmitted in the commentary's apparatus.]

Al-Farra' said regarding His saying, mighty and majestic: "tacolu minsa'atahu" is the great staff carried by the herdsman, taken from "nasa'tu al-ba'ir" when I drove the camel so that it would hasten its pace, as one says "nasa'tu al-laban" when I poured water on it, and it is "al-naseey".

Al-Farra' reported from Abu Ja'far al-Rawwasi that he asked Abu Amr about it, and he said: ﴿minsatahu﴾ without hamza.

The majority of the readers of Kufa recited ﴿minsa'atahu﴾ with hamza, and it seems they understood it as mif'ala from "nasa'tu al-ba'ir" when I drove it so that it would increase its pace, as one says "nasa'tu al-laban" when I poured water on it, which is "al-naseey", and as one says "nasa'a Allahu fi ajalika", meaning God prolonged the days of your life.

Abu Ja'far said: These are two readings, and scholars among the readers have read each of them with the same meaning; whichever one the reader recites is correct, though I prefer the hamza in it because it is the original form.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So when he fell, the jinn saw clearly﴾

He, mighty and majestic, says: When Solomon fell down to the ground upon the breaking of his staff, ﴿the jinn saw clearly that, had they known the unseen﴾ which they claimed to know, ﴿they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment﴾, the degrading one, for a full year after Solomon's death, while they thought Solomon was alive.

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

- Ahmad ibn Mansur told us, saying: Musa ibn Mas'ud Abu Hudhayfa told us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Tahman told us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Solomon, the Prophet of God, when he prayed, would see a tree growing before him, and he would say to it, 'What is your name?' It would say, 'such-and-such.' He would say, 'For what purpose are you?' If it was for planting, it would be planted; if it was for medicine, it would be recorded. Then one day while he was praying he saw a tree before him, and he said to it, 'What is your name?' It said, 'The carob tree.' He said, 'For what purpose are you?' It said, 'For the ruin of this house.' Solomon said, 'O God, conceal my death from the jinn, so that mankind may know that the jinn do not know the unseen.' He carved it into a staff and leaned on it for a year dead, while the jinn worked. The termite ate it, and he fell, and mankind clearly understood that had the jinn known the unseen, they would not have remained a year in the humiliating punishment." He said: Ibn Abbas used to recite it thus. He said: The jinn thanked the termite, and it would bring them water.

- Musa ibn Harun told us, saying: Amr told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, in a report he related from Abu Malik and from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, and from Murra al-Hamdani, from Ibn Mas'ud, and from some companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who said: "Solomon would seclude himself [in the context of al-Tha'labi's al-Ara'is] in Bayt al-Maqdis for a year or two years, a month or two months, and less or more than that, his food and drink being brought in. He entered it at the time he died, and that was because there was no morning on which he did not see a tree growing in it, and he would ask it, 'What is your name?' The tree would say, 'My name is such-and-such.' He would say to it, 'For what purpose did you grow?' It would say, 'I grew for such-and-such.' He would order it cut down; if it had grown for planting, he would plant it, and if it had grown as medicine, it would say, 'I grew as medicine for such-and-such,' and he would make it so. Then a tree grew called the carob, and he asked it, 'What is your name?' It said to him, 'I am the carob.' He said, 'For what purpose have you grown?' It said, 'For the ruin of this mosque.' Solomon said, 'God would not ruin it while I am alive. You are the one upon whose face is my destruction and the ruin of Bayt al-Maqdis.' He uprooted it and planted it in a wall of his, then entered the prayer niche and stood praying, leaning on his staff, and he died, and the devils did not know of it in that, while they were working for him, fearing that he would come out and punish them. The devils used to gather around the prayer niche, which had openings before and behind him. The devil who wanted to escape would say, 'Am I not a stout one? If I enter, I will come out from the other side.' One of those devils entered and passed through, and no devil looked at Solomon in the niche without being burned. He passed, and did not hear Solomon's voice; then he returned and did not hear it; then he returned and fell into the house and was not burned, and he saw Solomon had fallen, so he went out and informed the people that Solomon had died. They opened for him and brought him out, and they found his staff, which is the staff in the Abyssinian tongue, eaten by the termite, and they did not know how long he had been dead. They placed the termite upon the staff, and it ate from it for a day and a night. Then they calculated on that basis and found that he had died a year earlier." It is in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "They remained toiling for him after his death for a full year. Then the people were certain that the jinn had been lying to them, and that had they known the unseen, they would have known of Solomon's death and would not have remained a year in the punishment, working for him." And this is the saying of God: ﴿nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating away at his staff. So when he fell, the jinn saw clearly that, had they known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment.﴾ He says: their affair became clear to the people, that they had been lying to them. Then the devils said to the termite: "If you ate food, we would bring you the finest food; if you drank drink, we would give you the finest drink; but we will transport water and clay to you." So what is in the inside of the wood is what the devils bring to it in gratitude.

- Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, who said: "The jinn used to inform mankind that they knew some things of the unseen, and that they knew what would be tomorrow. Then they were tested by Solomon's death; he died and remained a year upon his staff, while they did not perceive his death, and they were subjugated that year, working tirelessly." ﴿So when he fell, the jinn saw clearly that, had they known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment.﴾ And they indeed remained toiling and working for him for a year.

- Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating away at his staff﴾: Solomon said to the Angel of Death, "O Angel of Death, when you are commanded concerning me, inform me." He came to him and said, "O Solomon, I have been commanded concerning you; a short while remains for you." He called the devils, and they built around him a palace of glass with no door. He stood praying and leaned on his staff. The Angel of Death came to him and seized his soul while he was leaning on his staff, and he did not do that in flight from the Angel of Death. The jinn were working before him and looking at him, thinking he was alive. God then sent the creature of the earth, a creature that eats wood called the "qadih", which entered it and ate it, until when it had eaten the inside of the staff it weakened, and its weight became too much for it, and it fell dead. When the jinn saw that, they dispersed and left. That is His saying ﴿nothing showed them his death except a creature of the earth eating away at his staff﴾. He said: al-minsa'a is the staff.

- Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Ata', who said: Solomon son of Dawud was praying, and he died while standing in prayer, and the jinn were working without knowing of his death, until the termite ate his staff and he fell.

As for "an" in His saying ﴿an law kanu﴾, it is in a position of raising (marfu') by "tabayyana" (became clear), because the meaning of the statement is: "When he fell, it became clear and manifest that had the jinn known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment."

As for the interpretation which Ibn Abbas gave, that its meaning is: "mankind saw clearly the jinn," then it would need to be in a position of accusative (nasb) by repeating it upon "al-jinn", and likewise on this reading the jinn would have to be in the accusative. However, I know of no reader among the readers of the major cities who reads it with jinn in the accusative, and if it were in the accusative, the word "tabayyanat" would contain a pronoun referring to mankind.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 15:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿There was for Sheba in their dwelling a sign: two gardens on the right and on the left. "Eat of the provision of your Lord and be grateful to Him. A good land and a Forgiving Lord."﴾ (15)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: There was indeed a clear sign for the descendants of Sheba in their dwelling, and a plain proof that they have no lord except the One who bestowed upon them the blessings in which they were.

Sheba, according to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), was the name of the father of Yemen.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Abu Hayyan al-Kalbi, from Yahya ibn Hani', from Urwa al-Muradi, from a man of them called Farwa ibn Musayk, who said: I said, "O Messenger of Allah, tell me about Sheba: what was it? A man or a woman, or a mountain or animals?" He said: "No, he was a man of the Arabs and had ten sons. Six of them went to the right (tayammun) and four went to the left (tasha'um). As for those who went right: Kinda, Himyar, al-Azd, al-Ash'ariyyun, Madhhij, and Anmar, from whom are Khath'am and Bujayla. As for those who went left: 'Amila, Judham, Lakhm, and Ghassan."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: Abu Sabra al-Nakha'i narrated to us, from Farwa ibn Musayk al-Qutay'i, who said: A man said, "O Messenger of Allah, tell me about Sheba: what is it? A land or a woman?" He said: "It is neither a land nor a woman, but a man who fathered ten children. Six went to the right and four went to the left. As for those who went left: Lakhm, Judham, 'Amila, and Ghassan; and as for those who went right: Kinda, al-Ash'ariyyun, al-Azd, Madhhij, Himyar, and Anmar." A man said, "What is Anmar?" He said: "Those from whom are Khath'am and Bujayla."

Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: al-'Anqazi narrated to us, saying: Asbat ibn Nasr informed me, from Yahya ibn Hani' al-Muradi, from his father or his paternal uncle, [Asbat is in doubt], who said: Farwa ibn Musayk came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, tell me about Sheba: was it a mountain or a land?" He said: "It was neither a mountain nor a land, but it was a man of the Arabs who fathered ten tribes," and he then mentioned something similar, except that he said: "And Anmar, those who are said to be from them are Bujayla and Khath'am." If the matter is as narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that Sheba is a man, then both the inflection (al-i'raj) and the non-inflection (ghayr al-i'raj) are acceptable: inflecting it treats it as the name of a known man, and not inflecting it treats it as the name of a tribe or a land. Scholars among the readers have recited with each of them.

The readers differed in the reading of His words ﴿fi maskanihim﴾. The majority of the readers of Madina and Basra, and some of the Kufans, read ﴿fi masakinihim﴾ in the plural, meaning the dwellings of the family of Sheba. The majority of the readers of Kufa read ﴿fi maskanihim﴾ in the singular, with a kasra on the kaf, and this is, as has been related to me, a dialect of the people of Yemen. Hamza read ﴿maskanihim﴾ in the singular with a fatha on the kaf.

The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is that all of these are readings close in meaning, so whichever reading the reader recites is correct.

* *

As for His words ﴿ayah﴾ (sign),

we have already explained its meaning earlier.

As for His words ﴿two gardens on the right and on the left﴾, it means: two gardens lying between two mountains, on the right and left of whoever came to them.

As for their kind, it has been related to us that:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Sulayman narrated to us, saying: Abu Hilal narrated to us, saying: I heard Qatada on His words ﴿Indeed there was for Sheba in their dwelling a sign: two gardens on the right and on the left﴾, he said: There were two gardens between two mountains. A woman would carry her basket on her head and walk between the two mountains, and her basket would be filled without her touching it with her hand. When they transgressed, Allah sent upon them a creature called "jurad" (a rat), which burrowed into them and drowned them, and nothing remained for them except tamarisk and a little lote-tree.

Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, on His words ﴿Indeed there was for Sheba in their dwelling a sign: two gardens on the right and on the left ...﴾ to His words ﴿so they turned away, and We sent upon them the flood of al-'Arim﴾: He said: No gnat, fly, flea, scorpion, or snake was ever seen in their town. Caravans would come with lice and vermin in their clothes, but as soon as they looked at their houses, the vermin would die. He said: A person would enter the two gardens, hold a basket on his head, and come out when he came out, and that basket would be full of all kinds of fruit, and he would not have taken any of it with his hand. He said: And the dam was irrigating them.

The two gardens in His words ﴿two gardens on the right and on the left﴾ are in apposition to the sign, because the meaning of the statement is: There was for Sheba in their dwelling a sign, namely two gardens on their right and their left.

* *

As for His words ﴿Eat of the provision of your Lord﴾,

it is what provides for you from these two gardens, from their crops and fruits, ﴿and be grateful to Him﴾ for what He has bestowed upon you of that provision. Here the report ends, and then a new report begins about the land, and it is said: "This is a good land," meaning it is not saline, but, as we have mentioned, it has the qualities described by Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, that there was nothing harmful in it: no insects, crawling creatures, or vermin, as Ibn Zayd described. ﴿And a Forgiving Lord﴾ means: a Lord who forgives your sins, if you obey Him.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, on His words ﴿a good land and a Forgiving Lord﴾: "and your Lord is Forgiving of your sins." A people whom Allah gave blessings, and commanded them to obey Him and forbade them from disobeying Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 34, verses 16–17:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿So they turned away, and We sent upon them the flood of the dam (sayl al-'Arim), and We replaced for them their two gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit, tamarisk, and a few lote-trees.﴾ [16] ﴿That was Our recompense for them because they disbelieved. And do We recompense any but the ungrateful?﴾ [17]

His, may He be remembered, saying means: Saba' turned away from obedience to their Lord and deviated from following what their messengers called them to, namely that He is their Creator.

As follows:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, from Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, who said: Allah sent to Saba' thirteen prophets, and they denied them. ﴿So We sent upon them the flood of the dam.﴾ His, may He be remembered, saying means: We breached their dam, which had been holding back the torrents from them, when they turned away from confirming Our messengers.

Al-'Arim is the embankment (musannah) that holds back water; its singular is 'arimah. It is this that al-A'sha referred to in his saying:

"So in that is an example for the one who takes warning, and Ma'rib, which the 'Arim has obliterated.
A dam which Himyar built for them; when its water came, it did not stop."

[The two verses are by al-A'sha of Banu Qays ibn Tha'labah (his Diwan, Cairo edition, p. 43), from a qasidah in praise of Qays ibn Ma'd Yakrib, in the meter al-Mutaqarib. In it, "qafa" appears in place of "afa," and "rakham" with a kha' in place of "rijam" with a jim. In some copies of the Diwan: "mawaruh" in place of "ma'uh." Al-Farra' said: His saying "the flood of the 'Arim": it was an embankment holding back water, with three gates in it. They would water from that water through the first gate (the upper), then the second (the middle), then the last (the lower), and it would not be exhausted until the water returned in the following year. They were the most comfortable people in livelihood, but when they turned away and denied the messengers, Allah breached that embankment upon them, so their land was flooded and the sand buried their houses. The two verses are among the evidences of Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an, and his narration reads "qafa" in place of "afa," which has the same meaning; and "rakham" with a kha' in place of rijam, and the rijam are great rocks, the plural of rijmah, placed on a grave or the like. His saying "lam yarim" is explained as: it did not hold back; the pronoun refers to the water. And he said concerning His saying, "the flood of the 'Arim": its singular is 'arimah, which is a structure like a mushan, by which water is held back, and it overlooks the water in the middle of the land, and passages are left in it for boats; those are the 'arimat, whose singular is 'arimah. End. In (al-Lisan, s-n-y) al-musannah is al-'arim. In (al-Lisan, '-r-m) al-'arim, with the ra' vocalized with fatha or kasra, and likewise its singular, which is al-'arimah, and al-'arim is a dam that blocks the valley; its plural is 'arim. It is said that al-'arim is a collective noun with no singular. Abu Hanifah said: al-'azm are the barriers built in the midst of valleys. End. And this is what we today call reservoirs or dams.]

It was said that the 'Arim, as has been mentioned, was built by Bilqis.

Those who said that:

⁕ Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi related to us, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir related to me, saying: My father related to us, saying: I heard al-Mughirah ibn Hakim say: When Bilqis became ruler, her people began fighting over the water of their valley. She began to forbid them, but they did not obey her, so she left her rule and went to one of her palaces and left them. When the evil among them increased and they regretted it, they came to her and urged her to return to her rule, but she refused. They said: "You must return, or we will kill you." She said: "You do not obey me, and you have no minds. Do not obey me." They said: "We will obey you, for we have found no good among us after you." So she came and ordered their valley, and it was dammed with the 'Arim.

Ahmad said: Wahb said: My father said: I asked al-Mughirah ibn Hakim about the 'Arim, and he said: In the language of Himyar it is the musannah. They dammed what lay between the two mountains, blocking the water behind the dam, and made gates for it, some above others, and built behind it a great reservoir, in which she made twelve outlets according to the number of their rivers. When the rain came, the torrent was held back behind the dam, and she ordered the upper gate opened, so its water flowed into the reservoir. She ordered dung to be thrown into it, and some of the dung came out faster than others, and those channels kept narrowing while she sent the dung into the water until all of it came out together. So she used to divide the water among them in this manner, until there came to pass what came to pass between her and Solomon.

⁕ Ahmad ibn 'Umar al-Basri related to us, saying: Abu Salih ibn Zuraiq related to us, saying: Shurayk related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Maysarah, concerning His saying ﴿So We sent upon them the flood of the 'Arim﴾, he said: al-musannah in the dialect of Yemen.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning Allah's saying ﴿the flood of the 'Arim﴾, he said: severe. And it was said: al-'Arim is the name of a valley that belonged to these people.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿So We sent upon them the flood of the 'Arim﴾, he said: a valley in Yemen which flowed toward Makkah, and they would irrigate from it, and its flood would reach there.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿So We sent upon them the flood of the 'Arim﴾: It was mentioned to us that the flood of the 'Arim was a valley to which the channels of various valleys gathered. They deliberately dammed what lay between the two mountains with pitch and stones and made gates upon it, and they would take from its water what they needed and block from themselves whatever they did not need from its water.

⁕ It was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying ﴿So We sent upon them the flood of the 'Arim﴾: a valley called al-'Arim; when it rained, the valleys of Yemen would flow to al-'Arim, and the water gathered there. Saba' deliberately dammed al-'Arim between the two mountains, blocking it with rock and pitch, and it remained blocked for a time, so they did not expect water, meaning they did not fear.

Others said: al-'Arim is a description of the embankment they had, not its name.

Those who said that:

⁕ 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿the flood of the 'Arim﴾, he said: the severe. The cause by which Allah brought that flood upon them, as was mentioned to me, was a rat that Allah sent against their dam, and it bored holes in it.

Then the people of knowledge differed concerning the manner of what occurred through that hole that caused the ruin of their two gardens.

Some of them said: The manner of it was that when the flood found an opening in the dam, it worked upon it; then the water overflowed onto their gardens, drowning them and ruining their land and dwellings.

Those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, from Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, who said: They, meaning Saba', had a dam which they had built as a permanent structure, and it was what held the flood back from them when it came to overrun their wealth. It was believed among them, according to their knowledge derived from their soothsayers, that their dam would only be ruined by a mouse. So they left no gap between two stones without tying a cat beside it. When its time came and Allah willed to drown them, there came, as they report, a red mouse to one of those cats and attacked it until the cat retreated from it, and it entered the gap that had been beside it, burrowed into the dam, and dug in it until it weakened it for the flood, while they did not know. When the flood came, it found a breach and entered it until it uprooted the dam and overflowed onto the wealth, carrying it away, so nothing remained of it except what Allah mentioned. When they dispersed, they settled under the soothsayers of 'Imran ibn 'Amir.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: When the people abandoned Allah's command, Allah sent against them a rat called al-Khuld, which bored into it from its base until their gardens were drowned by it and their land was ruined by it, as a punishment for their deeds.

⁕ Al-Husayn related to us, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: When they transgressed and rebelled, meaning Saba', Allah sent against them a rat which tore a hole in the dam for them, and Allah drowned them.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb related to us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Allah sent against it a rat and set it upon what held back the water that irrigated them, and it bored into the mouths of those stones and everything in them of lead and other things, until it left them as mere stones. Then Allah sent the flood of the 'Arim, which uprooted that dam and what it held back, and uprooted those two gardens and carried them away. He recited ﴿So We sent upon them the flood of the 'Arim, and We replaced for them their two gardens with two gardens﴾ and said: It carried away those villages and the two gardens.

Others said: The manner of it was that the water with which they irrigated their gardens flowed to a place other than the one from which they benefited, and that is why their gardens were ruined.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah sent against them, meaning against the 'Arim, a beast from the earth, which bored a hole in it, so that water flowed to a place other than the one from which they benefited. Allah replaced their two gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit, and that was when they disobeyed and grew insolent in their livelihood.

The first opinion is more consistent with what the apparent meaning of the revelation indicates, because Allah, may He be remembered, informed that He sent upon them the flood of the 'Arim, and sending it upon them would not occur except by its flowing over them or over their gardens and land, not by its being turned away from them.

* *

And His saying ﴿and We replaced for them their two gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit﴾

His, may He be remembered, saying means: In place of their orchards, We made for them orchards of the produce of the arak tree, and the arak is the khamt.

The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

⁕ 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah replaced for them their two gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit; and khamt is the arak.

⁕ Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', who said: I heard al-Hasan say concerning His saying ﴿bearing bitter fruit﴾: I think he said: khamt is the arak.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Ammarah related to me, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Musa related to me, saying: Isra'il related to us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, ﴿bearing bitter fruit﴾: khamt is the arak.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿bearing bitter fruit﴾: the arak.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿bearing bitter fruit﴾: khamt is the arak, and its fruit is the bitter berry.

⁕ It was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying ﴿And We replaced for them their two gardens with two gardens﴾: Allah replaced for them, in place of the gardens of fruits and grapes, when their gardens became khamt, which is the arak.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb related to us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿And We replaced for them their two gardens with two gardens﴾: He removed those villages and the two gardens, and replaced for them what He told you of: bearing bitter fruit. He said: khamt is the arak. He said: In place of grapes He made arak, and in place of fruit, athl and a few lote-trees.

The readers differed in the reading of this. The majority of the readers of the cities read "ukulin" with tanwin, except Abu 'Amr, who makes it genitive to khamt, meaning "possessors of khamt fruit." As for those who do not make it genitive to khamt and read the ukul with tanwin, they made khamt the ukul, and so made it agree with it in its i'rab (grammatical case). The readers of the cities read the alif and the kaf of "ukul" with a damma, except Nafi', who lightened it.

The correct reading in this matter, in my view, is the reading of those who read "dhawati ukul" with a damma on the alif and the kaf, because the readers of the authoritative community agree upon it, and with tanwin on ukul, because this reading is widely transmitted among the readers of the cities; without my seeing an error in the reading of one who reads it genitive to khamt. The same applies to making it genitive and not making it genitive, like the saying of the Arabs about the garden of so-and-so: "a'nabu karmin" and "a'nabun karmun," so that they sometimes make a'nab genitive to karm because it is from it, and sometimes give it tanwin, then translate it as karm, since grapes are the fruit of the vine.

As for athl: it is said to be the tamarisk (tarfa'), and it was said: a tree similar to the tamarisk but larger than it, and it was said: it is the samur (acacia).

Those who said that:

⁕ 'Ali related to me, saying: Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿and athl﴾: athl is the tarfa' (tamarisk).

* *

And His saying ﴿and a few lote-trees﴾

He says: possessors of khamt and athl and a little lote-tree.

Qatadah used to say concerning this:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to me, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿bearing bitter fruit, and tamarisk, and a few lote-trees﴾, he said: While the trees of the people were the best of trees, Allah turned them into the worst of trees because of their deeds.

* *

And His saying ﴿That was Our recompense for them because they disbelieved﴾

He, may He be remembered, says: This which We did to these people of Saba', by sending upon them the flood of the 'Arim, until their wealth was destroyed and their gardens ruined, was Our recompense for their disbelief in Us and their denial of Our messengers. The "dhalika" in His saying ﴿dhalika jazaynahum﴾ is in the accusative position, governed by "jazaynahum" upon it, and the meaning of the sentence is: We recompensed them that because they disbelieved.

* *

And His saying ﴿And do We recompense any but the ungrateful?﴾

The readers differed in reading it. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra and some of the people of Kufa read ﴿wa-hal yujza﴾ with the yaʼ and with fatha on the zay, in the passive form, ﴿illa al-kafur﴾ with raf' (nominative). The majority of the readers of Kufa read ﴿wa-hal nujazi﴾ with the nun and with kasra on the zay, ﴿illa al-kafura﴾ with nasb (accusative).

The correct view concerning this is that they are two well-known readings among the readers of the cities, close in meaning, and whichever one the reader recites is correct. The meaning of the sentence is: Thus We repaid them for their disbelief in Allah, and do we recompense any but the one who is ungrateful for Allah's blessing?

If someone says: Does Allah not recompense the people of faith in Him for their righteous deeds, so that the recompense is restricted to the people of disbelief? It is said: "Do we recompense any but the ungrateful?" It is said in reply: recompense in this place means requital, and Allah, may He be remembered, promised the people of faith in Him bounty upon them, and that for each one of their righteous deeds He would give them ten times its like, up to an unlimited multiplication; and He promised the evildoer among His servants that for each one of his misdeeds He would give a like punishment as requital for his sin. Requital (mukafa'ah) applies to the people of major sins and disbelief, while recompense (jaza') for the people of faith is accompanied by bounty. Therefore He, may His praise be exalted, said in this place ﴿And do We recompense any but the ungrateful?﴾, as if He, may His praise be exalted, said: None is requited for his deed except the ungrateful, when requital is like what was requited; and Allah does not forgive him any of his sins, nor is any of them expiated in this world.

As for the believer, bounty is bestowed upon him as I have described.

The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to us, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿And do We recompense﴾: We punish.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿That was Our recompense for them because they disbelieved, and do We recompense any but the ungrateful?﴾: Indeed Allah, when He wills kindness for His servant, accepts his good deeds, and when He wills humiliation for His servant, He holds back his sins against him until he is brought to account for them on the Day of Resurrection. He said: It was mentioned to us that a man, while on a road of Medina, a woman passed by him, and he followed her with his gaze until he came upon a wall and struck his face against it, so that his face was bleeding. He came to the Prophet of Allah, and his face was flowing with blood, and he said: "O Prophet of Allah, I did such and such." The Prophet of Allah said to him: "When Allah wills kindness for a servant, He hastens for him the punishment for his sin in this world, and when Allah wills humiliation for a servant, He holds back his sin against him until he is brought to account for it on the Day of Resurrection, as if he were a tailless mule."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 34, verses 16–17:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿So they turned away, and We sent upon them the flood of the dam (sayl al-'Arim), and We replaced for them their two gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit, tamarisk, and a few lote-trees.﴾ [16] ﴿That was Our recompense for them because they disbelieved. And do We recompense any but the ungrateful?﴾ [17]

His, may He be remembered, saying means: Saba' turned away from obedience to their Lord and deviated from following what their messengers called them to, namely that He is their Creator.

As follows:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, from Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, who said: Allah sent to Saba' thirteen prophets, and they denied them. ﴿So We sent upon them the flood of the dam.﴾ His, may He be remembered, saying means: We breached their dam, which had been holding back the torrents from them, when they turned away from confirming Our messengers.

Al-'Arim is the embankment (musannah) that holds back water; its singular is 'arimah. It is this that al-A'sha referred to in his saying:

"So in that is an example for the one who takes warning, and Ma'rib, which the 'Arim has obliterated.
A dam which Himyar built for them; when its water came, it did not stop."

[The two verses are by al-A'sha of Banu Qays ibn Tha'labah (his Diwan, Cairo edition, p. 43), from a qasidah in praise of Qays ibn Ma'd Yakrib, in the meter al-Mutaqarib. In it, "qafa" appears in place of "afa," and "rakham" with a kha' in place of "rijam" with a jim. In some copies of the Diwan: "mawaruh" in place of "ma'uh." Al-Farra' said: His saying "the flood of the 'Arim": it was an embankment holding back water, with three gates in it. They would water from that water through the first gate (the upper), then the second (the middle), then the last (the lower), and it would not be exhausted until the water returned in the following year. They were the most comfortable people in livelihood, but when they turned away and denied the messengers, Allah breached that embankment upon them, so their land was flooded and the sand buried their houses. The two verses are among the evidences of Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an, and his narration reads "qafa" in place of "afa," which has the same meaning; and "rakham" with a kha' in place of rijam, and the rijam are great rocks, the plural of rijmah, placed on a grave or the like. His saying "lam yarim" is explained as: it did not hold back; the pronoun refers to the water. And he said concerning His saying, "the flood of the 'Arim": its singular is 'arimah, which is a structure like a mushan, by which water is held back, and it overlooks the water in the middle of the land, and passages are left in it for boats; those are the 'arimat, whose singular is 'arimah. End. In (al-Lisan, s-n-y) al-musannah is al-'arim. In (al-Lisan, '-r-m) al-'arim, with the ra' vocalized with fatha or kasra, and likewise its singular, which is al-'arimah, and al-'arim is a dam that blocks the valley; its plural is 'arim. It is said that al-'arim is a collective noun with no singular. Abu Hanifah said: al-'azm are the barriers built in the midst of valleys. End. And this is what we today call reservoirs or dams.]

It was said that the 'Arim, as has been mentioned, was built by Bilqis.

Those who said that:

⁕ Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi related to us, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir related to me, saying: My father related to us, saying: I heard al-Mughirah ibn Hakim say: When Bilqis became ruler, her people began fighting over the water of their valley. She began to forbid them, but they did not obey her, so she left her rule and went to one of her palaces and left them. When the evil among them increased and they regretted it, they came to her and urged her to return to her rule, but she refused. They said: "You must return, or we will kill you." She said: "You do not obey me, and you have no minds. Do not obey me." They said: "We will obey you, for we have found no good among us after you." So she came and ordered their valley, and it was dammed with the 'Arim.

Ahmad said: Wahb said: My father said: I asked al-Mughirah ibn Hakim about the 'Arim, and he said: In the language of Himyar it is the musannah. They dammed what lay between the two mountains, blocking the water behind the dam, and made gates for it, some above others, and built behind it a great reservoir, in which she made twelve outlets according to the number of their rivers.
