When the rain came, the torrent was held back behind the dam, and she ordered the upper gate opened, so its water flowed into the reservoir. She ordered dung to be thrown into it, and some of the dung came out faster than others, and those channels kept narrowing while she sent the dung into the water until all of it came out together. So she used to divide the water among them in this manner, until there came to pass what came to pass between her and Solomon.

⁕ Ahmad ibn 'Umar al-Basri related to us, saying: Abu Salih ibn Zuraiq related to us, saying: Shurayk related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Maysarah, concerning His saying ﴿So We sent upon them the flood of the 'Arim﴾, he said: al-musannah in the dialect of Yemen.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning Allah's saying ﴿the flood of the 'Arim﴾, he said: severe. And it was said: al-'Arim is the name of a valley that belonged to these people.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿So We sent upon them the flood of the 'Arim﴾, he said: a valley in Yemen which flowed toward Makkah, and they would irrigate from it, and its flood would reach there.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿So We sent upon them the flood of the 'Arim﴾: It was mentioned to us that the flood of the 'Arim was a valley to which the channels of various valleys gathered. They deliberately dammed what lay between the two mountains with pitch and stones and made gates upon it, and they would take from its water what they needed and block from themselves whatever they did not need from its water.

⁕ It was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying ﴿So We sent upon them the flood of the 'Arim﴾: a valley called al-'Arim; when it rained, the valleys of Yemen would flow to al-'Arim, and the water gathered there. Saba' deliberately dammed al-'Arim between the two mountains, blocking it with rock and pitch, and it remained blocked for a time, so they did not expect water, meaning they did not fear.

Others said: al-'Arim is a description of the embankment they had, not its name.

Those who said that:

⁕ 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿the flood of the 'Arim﴾, he said: the severe. The cause by which Allah brought that flood upon them, as was mentioned to me, was a rat that Allah sent against their dam, and it bored holes in it.

Then the people of knowledge differed concerning the manner of what occurred through that hole that caused the ruin of their two gardens.

Some of them said: The manner of it was that when the flood found an opening in the dam, it worked upon it; then the water overflowed onto their gardens, drowning them and ruining their land and dwellings.

Those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq related to me, from Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani, who said: They, meaning Saba', had a dam which they had built as a permanent structure, and it was what held the flood back from them when it came to overrun their wealth. It was believed among them, according to their knowledge derived from their soothsayers, that their dam would only be ruined by a mouse. So they left no gap between two stones without tying a cat beside it. When its time came and Allah willed to drown them, there came, as they report, a red mouse to one of those cats and attacked it until the cat retreated from it, and it entered the gap that had been beside it, burrowed into the dam, and dug in it until it weakened it for the flood, while they did not know. When the flood came, it found a breach and entered it until it uprooted the dam and overflowed onto the wealth, carrying it away, so nothing remained of it except what Allah mentioned. When they dispersed, they settled under the soothsayers of 'Imran ibn 'Amir.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: When the people abandoned Allah's command, Allah sent against them a rat called al-Khuld, which bored into it from its base until their gardens were drowned by it and their land was ruined by it, as a punishment for their deeds.

⁕ Al-Husayn related to us, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: When they transgressed and rebelled, meaning Saba', Allah sent against them a rat which tore a hole in the dam for them, and Allah drowned them.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb related to us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Allah sent against it a rat and set it upon what held back the water that irrigated them, and it bored into the mouths of those stones and everything in them of lead and other things, until it left them as mere stones. Then Allah sent the flood of the 'Arim, which uprooted that dam and what it held back, and uprooted those two gardens and carried them away. He recited ﴿So We sent upon them the flood of the 'Arim, and We replaced for them their two gardens with two gardens﴾ and said: It carried away those villages and the two gardens.

Others said: The manner of it was that the water with which they irrigated their gardens flowed to a place other than the one from which they benefited, and that is why their gardens were ruined.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah sent against them, meaning against the 'Arim, a beast from the earth, which bored a hole in it, so that water flowed to a place other than the one from which they benefited. Allah replaced their two gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit, and that was when they disobeyed and grew insolent in their livelihood.

The first opinion is more consistent with what the apparent meaning of the revelation indicates, because Allah, may He be remembered, informed that He sent upon them the flood of the 'Arim, and sending it upon them would not occur except by its flowing over them or over their gardens and land, not by its being turned away from them.

* *

And His saying ﴿and We replaced for them their two gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit﴾

His, may He be remembered, saying means: In place of their orchards, We made for them orchards of the produce of the arak tree, and the arak is the khamt.

The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

⁕ 'Ali related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Allah replaced for them their two gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit; and khamt is the arak.

⁕ Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', who said: I heard al-Hasan say concerning His saying ﴿bearing bitter fruit﴾: I think he said: khamt is the arak.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Ammarah related to me, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Musa related to me, saying: Isra'il related to us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, ﴿bearing bitter fruit﴾: khamt is the arak.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿bearing bitter fruit﴾: the arak.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, ﴿bearing bitter fruit﴾: khamt is the arak, and its fruit is the bitter berry.

⁕ It was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying ﴿And We replaced for them their two gardens with two gardens﴾: Allah replaced for them, in place of the gardens of fruits and grapes, when their gardens became khamt, which is the arak.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb related to us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿And We replaced for them their two gardens with two gardens﴾: He removed those villages and the two gardens, and replaced for them what He told you of: bearing bitter fruit. He said: khamt is the arak. He said: In place of grapes He made arak, and in place of fruit, athl and a few lote-trees.

The readers differed in the reading of this. The majority of the readers of the cities read "ukulin" with tanwin, except Abu 'Amr, who makes it genitive to khamt, meaning "possessors of khamt fruit." As for those who do not make it genitive to khamt and read the ukul with tanwin, they made khamt the ukul, and so made it agree with it in its i'rab (grammatical case). The readers of the cities read the alif and the kaf of "ukul" with a damma, except Nafi', who lightened it.

The correct reading in this matter, in my view, is the reading of those who read "dhawati ukul" with a damma on the alif and the kaf, because the readers of the authoritative community agree upon it, and with tanwin on ukul, because this reading is widely transmitted among the readers of the cities; without my seeing an error in the reading of one who reads it genitive to khamt. The same applies to making it genitive and not making it genitive, like the saying of the Arabs about the garden of so-and-so: "a'nabu karmin" and "a'nabun karmun," so that they sometimes make a'nab genitive to karm because it is from it, and sometimes give it tanwin, then translate it as karm, since grapes are the fruit of the vine.

As for athl: it is said to be the tamarisk (tarfa'), and it was said: a tree similar to the tamarisk but larger than it, and it was said: it is the samur (acacia).

Those who said that:

⁕ 'Ali related to me, saying: Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning ﴿and athl﴾: athl is the tarfa' (tamarisk).

* *

And His saying ﴿and a few lote-trees﴾

He says: possessors of khamt and athl and a little lote-tree.

Qatadah used to say concerning this:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to me, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿bearing bitter fruit, and tamarisk, and a few lote-trees﴾, he said: While the trees of the people were the best of trees, Allah turned them into the worst of trees because of their deeds.

* *

And His saying ﴿That was Our recompense for them because they disbelieved﴾

He, may He be remembered, says: This which We did to these people of Saba', by sending upon them the flood of the 'Arim, until their wealth was destroyed and their gardens ruined, was Our recompense for their disbelief in Us and their denial of Our messengers. The "dhalika" in His saying ﴿dhalika jazaynahum﴾ is in the accusative position, governed by "jazaynahum" upon it, and the meaning of the sentence is: We recompensed them that because they disbelieved.

* *

And His saying ﴿And do We recompense any but the ungrateful?﴾

The readers differed in reading it. The majority of the readers of Medina and Basra and some of the people of Kufa read ﴿wa-hal yujza﴾ with the yaʼ and with fatha on the zay, in the passive form, ﴿illa al-kafur﴾ with raf' (nominative). The majority of the readers of Kufa read ﴿wa-hal nujazi﴾ with the nun and with kasra on the zay, ﴿illa al-kafura﴾ with nasb (accusative).

The correct view concerning this is that they are two well-known readings among the readers of the cities, close in meaning, and whichever one the reader recites is correct. The meaning of the sentence is: Thus We repaid them for their disbelief in Allah, and do we recompense any but the one who is ungrateful for Allah's blessing?

If someone says: Does Allah not recompense the people of faith in Him for their righteous deeds, so that the recompense is restricted to the people of disbelief? It is said: "Do we recompense any but the ungrateful?" It is said in reply: recompense in this place means requital, and Allah, may He be remembered, promised the people of faith in Him bounty upon them, and that for each one of their righteous deeds He would give them ten times its like, up to an unlimited multiplication; and He promised the evildoer among His servants that for each one of his misdeeds He would give a like punishment as requital for his sin. Requital (mukafa'ah) applies to the people of major sins and disbelief, while recompense (jaza') for the people of faith is accompanied by bounty. Therefore He, may His praise be exalted, said in this place ﴿And do We recompense any but the ungrateful?﴾, as if He, may His praise be exalted, said: None is requited for his deed except the ungrateful, when requital is like what was requited; and Allah does not forgive him any of his sins, nor is any of them expiated in this world.

As for the believer, bounty is bestowed upon him as I have described.

The people of interpretation have said the like of what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to us, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿And do We recompense﴾: We punish.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿That was Our recompense for them because they disbelieved, and do We recompense any but the ungrateful?﴾: Indeed Allah, when He wills kindness for His servant, accepts his good deeds, and when He wills humiliation for His servant, He holds back his sins against him until he is brought to account for them on the Day of Resurrection. He said: It was mentioned to us that a man, while on a road of Medina, a woman passed by him, and he followed her with his gaze until he came upon a wall and struck his face against it, so that his face was bleeding. He came to the Prophet of Allah, and his face was flowing with blood, and he said: "O Prophet of Allah, I did such and such." The Prophet of Allah said to him: "When Allah wills kindness for a servant, He hastens for him the punishment for his sin in this world, and when Allah wills humiliation for a servant, He holds back his sin against him until he is brought to account for it on the Day of Resurrection, as if he were a tailless mule."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 18:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed, towns in plain view, and We determined the stages of travel among them: "Travel among them by night and by day in security."﴾ (34:18)

Exalted is He, mentioning His favour which He had bestowed upon these people who wronged themselves, says: And We placed between their land and the towns which We had blessed, namely Syria (al-Sham), towns in plain view.

Those who engage in interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, who said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿the towns which We had blessed﴾: He said, "Syria."

Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed﴾: meaning Syria.

'Ali ibn Sahl related to me, who said: Hajjaj related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿the towns which We had blessed﴾: He said, "Syria."

It has also been said: By the towns which were blessed is meant Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem).

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, who said: My father related to me, who said: My paternal uncle related to me, who said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed, towns in plain view﴾: He said, "The land which We had blessed is the holy land."

* *

As for His saying ﴿towns in plain view﴾:

Meaning: towns that are connected, and they are Arab towns.

Those who engage in interpretation have said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Ya'qub related to me, who said: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', who said: I heard al-Hasan regarding His saying ﴿And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed, towns in plain view﴾: He said, "Towns that are contiguous. One of them would set out in the morning and take his midday rest in one town, and go out in the evening and lodge in another town." He said: "A woman would place her basket on her head and busy herself with her spindle, and she would not return to her house until it was filled with all kinds of fruit."

Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿towns in plain view﴾: i.e., contiguous.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, who said: My father related to me, who said: My paternal uncle related to me, who said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿towns in plain view﴾: meaning Arab towns between Medina and Syria.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, who said: Abu 'Asim related to me, who said: 'Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, who said: al-Hasan related to us, who said: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿towns in plain view﴾: He said, "The sarawat" (the elevated lands/heights).

It was related from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying ﴿towns in plain view﴾: meaning Arab towns, and they were between Medina and Syria.

Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed, towns in plain view﴾: "Between their town and the towns of Syria there were towns in plain view. A woman would go out with her spindle and her basket on her head, and would set out from one town and reach another, and spend the night in a town, without carrying provisions or water, because of what lay between it and Syria."

* *

As for His saying ﴿And We determined the stages of travel among them﴾:

Exalted is He, mentioning, means: And We placed between their towns and the towns which We had blessed a determined journey, from station to station and from town to town; they would not rest except in a town, nor set out except from a town.

* *

As for His saying ﴿"Travel among them by night and by day in security"﴾:

He says: And We said to them, "Travel in these towns that lie between your towns and the towns which We had blessed, by night and by day, in security, not fearing hunger or thirst, nor injustice from anyone."

Those who engage in interpretation have said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿Travel among them by night and by day in security﴾: "They did not fear injustice or hunger. They would set out in the morning and take their midday rest, and go out in the evening and lodge in a town of people of gardens and rivers, to the extent that we have been told that a woman would place her basket on her head and busy herself with her hand, and her basket would be filled with fruit before she returned to her family, without having plucked anything. A man would travel carrying neither provisions nor water-skin, of what was spread out for the people."

Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿and by day in security﴾: "There was no fear in it."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 19:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So they said, "Our Lord, make distant the stages of our journey," and they wronged themselves, so We made them narratives and tore them completely apart. Indeed in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful one.﴾ (19)

The readers differed over the recitation of His saying ﴿Rabbana baa'id bayna asfarina﴾. The majority of the readers of Madina and Kufa recited it ﴿Rabbana baa'id bayna asfarina﴾ in the form of supplication and request, with the alif. Some readers of Makka and Basra recited ﴿ba'\u0080\u0080id﴾ with a shaddah on the 'ayn, also as a supplication. It is reported from earlier authorities that one of them recited ﴿Rabbana ba'ada bayna asfarina﴾ in the form of a statement from God that God did that to them. It is related from another that he recited ﴿Rabbana ba''ada﴾ also in the form of a statement, except that "Rabb" is in the vocative.

The correct recitation in our view is ﴿Rabbana baa'id﴾ and ﴿ba''id﴾, because they are the two well-known recitations among the recitation of the regional centres, and whatever is other than them is not known among them. Moreover, the people of interpretation also confirm the recitation of the one who recited it in the form of supplication and request, and this too further distances the other recitation from correctness.

Given that this is the correct recitation, the meaning of the speech is: "So they said: O our Lord, make distant the stages of our journey; so place between us and Syria deserts and wastelands, so that we may ride the mounts in them and take provisions with us in them." This shows the insolence of the people regarding God's blessing upon them and His kindness to them, and their ignorance of the value of well-being. Their Lord hastened to them the answer, just as He hastened it for those who said ﴿If this is the truth from You, then rain down on us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment﴾. He gave them what they desired and asked for in their request.

Those who interpret the Qur'an said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Abu Husayn Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to me, saying: 'Abthar narrated to us, saying: Husayn narrated to us from Abu Malik regarding this verse ﴿So they said, "Our Lord, make distant the stages of our journey"﴾. He said: They had villages connected in Yemen, some of which could see others, so they grew insolent over that and said: "Our Lord, make distant the stages of our journey." He said: So God sent upon them the flood of al-Arim, and made their food acacia, tamarisk, and a little lote-tree.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying ﴿So they said, "Our Lord, make distant the stages of our journey, and they wronged themselves"﴾. He said: They grew insolent about their livelihood and said: "If only the fruit of our gardens were farther away, it would be more fitting that we desire it." So they were torn apart between Syria and Saba, and in place of their two gardens they were given two gardens bearing bitter produce, acacia, and a little lote-tree.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding ﴿So they said, "Our Lord, make distant the stages of our journey"﴾: The people grew insolent toward God's blessing and disdained God's generosity. God said ﴿and they wronged themselves, so We made them narratives﴾.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿So they said, "Our Lord, make distant the stages of our journey"﴾: so that we may spend the night in the deserts and wildernesses. ﴿So they wronged themselves﴾.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and they wronged themselves﴾:

Their wronging of themselves was their doing what displeases God by His acts of disobedience, which necessitates God's punishment for them. ﴿So We made them narratives﴾: that is, We made them tales for people, whose example is struck in cursing; so it is said: "The people were scattered like the hands of Saba'," for "the hands of Saba'" means when they dispersed and were cut off.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and We tore them completely apart﴾:

That is, He cut them off throughout the lands, every severing.

As related:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding ﴿and they wronged themselves, so We made them narratives and tore them completely apart﴾: Qatada said: Amir al-Sha'bi said: As for Ghassan, they joined Syria; as for the Ansar, they joined Yathrib; as for Khuza'a, they joined Tihama; as for al-Azd, they joined Oman.

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: They claim that Imran ibn Amir, who was the uncle of the people, was a soothsayer, and he saw in his soothsaying that his people would be torn apart and scattered. So he said to them: "I have known that you will be torn apart. So whoever among you has a distant concern, a strong camel, and a new water-skin, let him join Ka's or Karud." So Wada'a ibn Amr went, and whoever among them had a sorrowful concern, a weak frame, and a worn-out water-skin, let him join the land of Shann; so it was 'Awf ibn Amr, who are called Bariq. And whoever among you wants a flourishing life and a secure sanctuary, let him join al-Arzin; so it was Khuza'a. And whoever wants the firm mountains in mud and the feeders in drought, let him join Yathrib of the palm trees; so it was al-Aws and al-Khazraj, and these are the two tribes of the Ansar. And whoever wants wine, dates, gold, silk, kingship and command, let him join Kawsa and Basra; so it was Ghassan, the sons of Jafna, kings of Syria, and whoever was among them in Iraq. Ibn Ishaq said: I have heard some people of knowledge say: this saying was uttered by Tarifa, the wife of Imran ibn Amir, who was a soothsayer, and she saw that in her soothsaying; and God knows best which of these was the case. He said: When they dispersed, they settled at the soothsaying of Imran ibn Amir.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful one﴾:

May His remembrance be exalted, He says: Indeed in Our tearing them apart completely are signs, that is, admonition, lesson, and indication of the obligation upon the servant of God's right to give thanks for His blessings when He bestows them, and His right to patience in His trial when He tests him with affliction, for every steadfast, grateful one for His blessings.

Those who interpret the Qur'an said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding ﴿Indeed in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful one﴾: Mutarrif used to say: What an excellent servant is the steadfast, grateful one, who when given gives thanks, and when tested is patient.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 20:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And Iblis had indeed proven true his assumption about them, so they followed him, except for a party of the believers﴾

The reciters differed over the recitation of His words ﴿And Iblis had indeed proven true his assumption about them﴾. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read ﴿ṣaddaqa﴾ with a doubled dal from ṣaddaqa (to confirm, to verify), meaning that he spoke an assumption (ẓann) of his, ﴿And you will not find most of them grateful﴾, and he said ﴿By Your might, I will surely mislead them all, except Your sincere servants among them﴾. Then his assumption about them came true, so it was realized in them, through their following him. The majority of the reciters of Madina, Syria and Basra read ﴿ṣadaqa﴾ with a single dal, meaning: and Iblis's assumption about them proved true.

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that both are well-known recitations, close in meaning. This is because Iblis did indeed prove true, concerning the disbelievers among the children of Adam, his assumption, and his assumption that he held when he said: ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left, and You will not find most of them grateful﴾, and when he said ﴿I will surely mislead them and I will surely arouse in them desires...﴾ the verse. The enemy of Allah said this as an assumption, thinking that he would do so, not as knowledge. So it became true through their following him. Whichever of the two recitations the reciter reads, he is correct.

If that is so, the meaning of the statement according to the reading of the one who reads with a doubled dal is: Iblis assumed about these people, whom We exchanged for their two gardens two gardens bearing bitter fruit, as a punishment from Us upon them, an assumption that was not certain, that they would follow him and obey him in disobeying Allah. So his assumption about them came true by his misleading them, until they obeyed him and disobeyed their Lord, except for a party of the believers in Allah, for they remained steadfast in obeying Allah and disobeying Iblis.

The people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

- Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us from Harun, who said: Amr ibn Malik informed me, from Abu al-Jawza, from Ibn Abbas, that he read ﴿And Iblis had indeed proven true his assumption about them﴾ with a doubled dal, and said: He assumed an assumption, and so his assumption came true.

- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿And Iblis had indeed proven true his assumption about them﴾, he said: He assumed an assumption, so they followed his assumption.

- He said: Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And Iblis had indeed proven true his assumption about them﴾, he said: Allah said: It was only an assumption he held, and Allah does not confirm a liar nor call a truthful one a liar.

- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿And Iblis had indeed proven true his assumption about them﴾: Have you seen these whom I honored over Me, and favored, and ennobled, that you will not find most of them grateful? And that was an assumption of his without knowledge. So Allah said ﴿so they followed him, except for a party of the believers﴾.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 34, verses 21–22:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And he had no authority over them except that We might make evident who believes in the Hereafter from who is in doubt about it. And your Lord is Guardian over all things.﴾ (21)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: Iblis had no proof with which to mislead these people whose description has been given, except that We empowered him over them, so that Our party and Our allies might be known: ﴿who believes in the Hereafter﴾, meaning: who affirms the resurrection, the reward and the punishment, ﴿from who is in doubt about it﴾, meaning: who does not have certainty about the return and does not affirm reward or punishment.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Basher narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿And he had no authority over them﴾, he said: al-Hasan said: "By Allah, he did not strike them with a staff, nor a sword, nor a whip, except with false desires and deceptions to which he invited them."

He said: Sa'id narrated to us from Qatada regarding His saying ﴿except that We might make evident who believes in the Hereafter from who is in doubt about it﴾, he said: "It was only a trial, so that Allah might know the believer from the disbeliever." It has also been said: by His saying ﴿except that We might make evident who believes in the Hereafter﴾ is meant: except that We might know that existing and manifest, so that by it they deserve reward or punishment.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And your Lord is Guardian over all things﴾:

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: And your Lord, O Muhammad, is over the deeds of these disbelievers in Him and over all other things ﴿Guardian﴾, nothing of it escapes His knowledge, and He will recompense all of them on the Day of Resurrection for what they earned in the world of good and evil.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Call upon those you claimed besides Allah; they do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, and they have no share in them, and He has no supporter among them.﴾ (22)

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: Thus is Our action toward Our friends and those who obeyed Us, David and Solomon, whose favours We bestowed upon them, blessings for which there is no equal, since they gave thanks; and that is Our action toward Sheba, whom We dealt with, when they grew insolent toward Our blessing, denied Our messengers, and disbelieved Our bounties. So say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists among your people who deny Our blessings upon them: Call upon, O people, those whom you claim to be partners with Allah besides Him; ask them to do for you some of Our actions toward those whose affairs We have described, whether bestowal or withdrawal. If they are unable to do that, then know that you are falsifiers, since partnership in lordship is neither valid nor permissible. Then He described those who are called upon besides Allah, saying: they do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, neither of good nor of harm nor of injury nor of benefit. How then could one who is like this be a god?

* *

As for His saying ﴿And they have no share in them﴾:

His saying, exalted is His remembrance: Nor do they, since they do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or the earth, have ownership of it independently apart from Allah, nor do they possess it by way of partnership, because ownership of owned things can only belong to their owner in one of two ways: either divided, or undivided. He says: their gods whom they call upon besides Allah do not possess the weight of an atom in the heavens or on the earth, neither divided nor undivided. How then could one who is thus be a partner to the One who has ownership of all of that?

* *

As for His saying ﴿And He has no supporter among them﴾:

He says: and the gods whom they call upon besides Him are not helpers of Allah in creating anything of that, nor in preserving it, since they had no ownership of any part of it, undivided or divided, so that it could be said: he is a partner to Him because he assisted, even though he had no ownership of any part of it.

Ahl al-ta'wil have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Basher narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying ﴿Say: Call upon those you claimed besides Allah; they do not possess an atom's weight in the heavens or on the earth, and they have no share in them﴾, he said: "There is no partner of Allah in heaven or on earth." ﴿And He has no supporter among them﴾, from those who are called upon besides Allah, ﴿from supporter﴾, meaning: from help in anything.

The Interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And intercession does not benefit with Him except for one whom He permits, until, when terror is removed from their hearts, they say, "What has your Lord said?" They say, "The truth; and He is the Most High, the Most Great."﴾ (34:23)

The Exalted says: Intercession by any intercessor, whoever he may be, does not benefit the one for whom intercession is made, except that it be made for one whom God has permitted to be interceded for. The Exalted says: If intercessions do not benefit anyone with God except for one for whom God has permitted intercession, and God does not permit any of His friends to intercede for any of the disbelievers in Him—and you are a people of disbelief in Him, O polytheists—then how can you worship those whom you worship besides God, supposing that you worship them so that they may bring you near to God in nearness and intercede for you with your Lord? So "man" (من) here, given that this is the meaning of the speech, in His words ﴿except for one whom He permits﴾ refers to the one for whom intercession is made.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words ﴿أُذِنَ لَهُ﴾ ( udhina lahu). The majority of readers recited it with a ḍamma on the alif, in the passive form (mā lam yusammi fā‛iluhu, "the passive whose agent is not named"). Some of the Kufans recited it as ﴿أَذِنَ لَهُ﴾ (adhina lahu), with a different report from him on this, meaning "God gave him permission."

And His words ﴿until, when terror is removed from their hearts﴾

He says: until, when they are relieved of terror in their hearts and it is lifted from them and departs.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the like of what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

Ali related to me, he said: Abu Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiya related to me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿until, when terror is removed from their hearts﴾: meaning, "uncovered" (juliya).

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, concerning ﴿until, when terror is removed from their hearts﴾: he said, "The veil is lifted from them on the Day of Resurrection."

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, on the authority of Qatada, who said: "When it is uncovered from their hearts."

The people of interpretation differed concerning who are described by this attribute, and what is the cause for which terror is removed from their hearts. Some of them said: those from whose hearts terror is removed are the angels. They said: terror is removed from their hearts only after a stupor that afflicts them when they hear God speak by revelation.

Mention of those who said that:

Yaqub related to me, he said: Ibn Ulayya related to us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of al-Sha'bi, who said: Ibn Mas'ud said concerning this verse, ﴿until, when terror is removed from their hearts﴾: He said: "When a matter occurs in the presence of the Lord of the Throne, those beneath Him among the angels hear a sound like the dragging of a chain over rock, and they are struck senseless. When terror has departed from their hearts, they call out to one another: ﴿What has your Lord said?﴾" He said: "So He says: whoever wills, let him say, 'The truth; and He is the Most High, the Most Great.'"

Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: al-Mu'tamir related to us, he said: I heard Dawud, on the authority of Amir, on the authority of Masruq, who said: "When a matter occurs in the presence of the Lord of the Throne, the angels hear a sound like the dragging of a chain over rock." He said: "They are struck senseless, and when terror is removed from their hearts they say: What has your Lord said?" He said: "He says, whom God wills: the truth; and He is the Most High, the Most Great."

Ibn al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abd al-A'la related to me, he said: Dawud related to us, on the authority of Amir, on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, that he said: "When a matter occurs in the presence of the Lord of the Throne," then he mentioned something similar in meaning, except that he said: "They are struck senseless from terror, until when that departs from them they call out: What has your Lord said?"

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, concerning His words ﴿until, when terror is removed from their hearts﴾: He said: "When the revelation is cast down, the people of the heavens hear a clanging like the clanging of a chain on smooth stones." He said: "They call out to one another in the heavens: What has your Lord said? And they call back: The truth; and He is the Most High, the Most Great."

And from him, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Abu al-Duha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah, the like of it.

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Ya'qub related to us, on the authority of Ja'far, on the authority of Sa'id, who said: "The command descends from the Lord of Might to the lowest heaven; so the people of the lowest heaven are terrified, until the matter for which it was sent down becomes clear to them. Then some of them say to others: What has your Lord said? And they answer: He has said the truth, and He is the Most High, the Most Great." This is His words ﴿until, when terror is removed from their hearts...﴾ the verse.

Ahmad ibn Abdah al-Dabbi related to us, he said: Sufyan ibn Uyayna related to us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ikrima, who said: Abu Hurayra related to us, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "When God decrees a matter in heaven, the angels strike their wings together, out of submission to His word, like the sound of a chain on smooth rock. That is His words ﴿until, when terror is removed from their hearts, they say, "What has your Lord said?" They say, "The truth; and He is the Most High, the Most Great."﴾"

Yaqub related to me, he said: Ibn Ulayya related to us, he said: Ayyub related to us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwa, who said: al-Harith ibn Hisham said to the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "How does revelation come to you?" He said: "It comes to me with a ringing like the ringing of a bell, and it departs from me when it departs, and I have retained what it said. And it sometimes comes in the form of a man, and he speaks to me, and it is easier for me."

Zakariyya ibn Aban al-Misri related to me, he said: Nu'aym related to us, he said: al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid ibn Jabir, on the authority of Ibn Abi Zakariyya, on the authority of Jabir ibn Hayya, on the authority of al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "When God wills to reveal a matter, He speaks the revelation, and the heavens are seized by a tremor, or he said a trembling, a severe fear of God's command. When the people of the heavens hear that, they swoon and fall prostrate to God. The first to raise his head will be Gabriel, and God speaks to him of His revelation what He wills. Then Gabriel passes by the angels; every time he passes a heaven, its angels ask him: What has our Lord said, O Gabriel? And Gabriel says: He has said the truth, and He is the Most High, the Most Great. They all then say the same as what Gabriel said, and Gabriel carries the revelation to where God commanded him."

I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words ﴿until, when terror is removed from their hearts...﴾ the verse: Ibn Abbas used to say: When God wished to reveal to Muhammad, He summoned Gabriel. When the Lord spoke the revelation, its sound was like the sound of iron on rock. When the people of the heavens heard the sound of the iron, they fell prostrate. When Gabriel came to them with the message, they raised their heads and said: ﴿What has your Lord said?﴾ ﴿They say, "The truth; and He is the Most High, the Most Great."﴾ This is the speech of the angels.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, concerning His words ﴿until, when terror is removed from their hearts...﴾ to ﴿and He is the Most High, the Most Great.﴾ He said: When God, the Exalted, revealed to Muhammad (ﷺ), He summoned the messenger from among the angels and sent the revelation. The angels heard the voice of the Almighty speaking the revelation. When it was uncovered from their hearts, they asked what God had said. They said: "The truth," and they knew that God says only the truth and that He fulfils what He promised. Ibn Abbas said: The sound of the revelation is like the sound of iron on rock; when they heard it they fell prostrate. When they raised their heads: ﴿They say, "What has your Lord said?" They say, "The truth; and He is the Most High, the Most Great."﴾ Then God commanded His Prophet to ask the people: ﴿Say: Who provides for you from the heavens...﴾ to His words ﴿in manifest error.﴾

Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu Amir related to us, he said: Qurra related to us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, concerning His words ﴿until, when terror is removed from their hearts...﴾ the verse, he said: The revelation descends from heaven, and when it has been completed, ﴿they say, "What has your Lord said?" They say, "The truth; and He is the Most High, the Most Great."﴾

Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Jarir related to us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah concerning His words ﴿until, when terror is removed from their hearts﴾: He said: "When the revelation is decreed in the corners of the heaven, it is like the striking of steel on stone. They become fearful, not knowing what has happened, and they are terrified. When the messengers pass by them, they say: ﴿What has your Lord said?﴾ They say: ﴿The truth; and He is the Most High, the Most Great.﴾"

Others, among those who said this, said: The ones described by this are the angels, and their terror is removed from their hearts only because of the decree of God which He issues, out of fear that it might be the establishment of the Hour.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, on the authority of Qatada, concerning His words ﴿until, when terror is removed from their hearts, they say, "What has your Lord said?"...﴾ the verse: He said: God reveals to Gabriel, and the angels scatter, or are terrified lest something of the matter of the Hour has occurred. When it is uncovered from their hearts and they know that it is not a matter of the Hour, ﴿they say, "What has your Lord said?" They say, "The truth; and He is the Most High, the Most Great."﴾

Others said: Rather, this is the action of the angels of the heavens when the angels who follow one another pass by them, out of fear that a matter of the Hour has occurred.

Mention of those who said that:

I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words ﴿until, when terror is removed from their hearts...﴾ the verse: Ibn Mas'ud claimed that the angels who follow one another, who go down to the earth to record deeds, when the Lord sends them and they descend, a loud sound is heard from them, so those beneath them among the angels think it is a matter of the Hour, and they fall prostrate. And so, whenever they pass by them, they do this out of fear of their Lord.

Others said: Rather, those described by this are the polytheists, and it is only the Satan from whose hearts terror is removed. They said: They only say "What has your Lord said?" at the descent of death upon them.

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿until, when terror is removed from their hearts﴾: "The fear of Satan is removed from their hearts; he departs from them, and his wishes and what used to mislead them. ﴿They say, "What has your Lord said?" They say, "The truth; and He is the Most High, the Most Great."﴾" He said: This is about the children of Adam, and it is at death: they acknowledge it when acknowledgement no longer benefits them.

The most correct of these sayings, in our view, is the one related by al-Sha'bi from Ibn Mas'ud, because of the soundness of the report we have mentioned from Ibn Abbas from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), which supports it. Since this is so, the meaning of the speech is: intercession does not benefit with Him except for one for whom He has permitted that intercession be made. So when God permits the one whom He permits to intercede, the people of the heavens are struck with terror on hearing His permission. Until, when terror is removed from their hearts and it is uncovered and lifted from them, they say: "What has your Lord said?" The angels say: "The truth," ﴿and He is the Most High﴾ over everything, ﴿the Most Great﴾ beside whom there is nothing.

The Arabs use "fuzzi'a" (فُزِّع) in two senses. They say of the brave man, through whom the matters that cause fear are brought down: "he is mufazza'" (مفزَّع). And they say of the coward who is frightened of everything: "indeed he is mufazza'" as well. Likewise they say of a man who, in disputes, prevails over his opponent: "he is mughallib" (مغلِّب), and when this meaning is intended he is ghalib (غالب). It is mentioned that Mujahid recited it ﴿fuzi‘a﴾, meaning: God removed the terror from them.

The correct recitation in this matter is the recitation with zay and ‘ayn, because of the consensus of the authoritative readers and the people of interpretation upon it, and because of the soundness of the report we have mentioned from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) supporting it, and indicating its soundness.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Say: Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth? Say: Allah. And indeed, either we or you are upon guidance or in clear error.﴾ (34:24)

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who associate idols and images with their Lord: Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth, by His sending down rain upon you from them, which is life for your crops and the sound condition of your livelihoods, and by His subjecting the sun, the moon and the stars for your benefit and the benefit of your sustenance; and from the earth, by His bringing forth from it your provisions and the provisions of your livestock. He omitted the report of the people's answer, relying on the indication of the speech upon it, and then mentioned it, which is: If they say, "We do not know," then say: "It is Allah who provides you with that." ﴿And indeed, either we or you, O people, are upon guidance or in clear error.﴾ Meaning: say to them: "Indeed we are upon guidance or in error, or you are upon error or guidance."

Ahl al-ta'wil (the exegetes) have said the same as what we have said concerning this.

And some people have said: the meaning of that is: "Indeed we are upon guidance, and indeed you are in clear error."

The scholars of Arabic differed concerning the reason for the use of "aw" (or) in this place. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: this does not indicate doubt; rather, it is in the speech of the Arabs such that it means he is the one who is guided. He said: a man may say to his slave, "One of us is striking his companion," and there is no confusion for the listener that the master is the one striking.

Another of them said: the meaning is: "Indeed we are upon guidance, and indeed you, you are in clear error," because the Arabs place "aw" in the position of the conjunctive waw (wāw al-muwalāh). Jarir said:

[The verse is by Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali. God, the One who is mentioned, says: ﴿Those who were arrogant﴾ in the world, and became leaders in misguidance and disbelief in God, ﴿to those who were oppressed﴾ in it, who were followers of the people of misguidance among them, when they said to them, ﴿Had it not been for you, we would have been believers﴾: ﴿Was it we who barred you from guidance﴾ and prevented you from following the truth ﴿after it had come to you﴾ from God, making it clear to you? ﴿Rather, you were criminals﴾: it was your preference for disbelief in God over faith that prevented you from following guidance and believing in God and His Messenger.

* *

The interpretation of the words of God, the Exalted: ﴿And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Rather, it was the scheming of the night and the day when you commanded us to disbelieve in God and set up rivals to Him." And they will conceal their regret when they see the punishment. We will place shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾ (33)

God, the One who is mentioned, says: ﴿And those who were oppressed﴾ from among the disbelievers in God in the world, who were followers of their leaders in misguidance, will say ﴿to those who were arrogant﴾ in it, who were their leaders: ﴿Rather, the scheming﴾ of you against us ﴿by the night and the day﴾ diverted us from guidance ﴿when you commanded us to disbelieve in God and set up for Him﴾ equals and likenesses in worship and divinity. The attribution to the night and the day is made, the meaning being what we have mentioned: the scheming of the arrogant against the oppressed during the night and the day. This is in accordance with the breadth of Arab speech in what its meaning is known from their discourse, namely the transfer of the attribute of one thing to another. You say to a man: "O so-and-so, your day is fasting and your night is standing," and as the poet said:

"You slept, while the night of the travelers is not sleeping" [[This is the second half of a verse by Jarir ibn Atiyya al-Khatafi, the Islamic poet, whose first half is: "You have blamed us, O Umm Ghaylan, for travelling by night." (His Diwan, Sawi edition, p. 554). The author cited it to show that you say "O so-and-so, your day is fasting and your night is standing," attributing fasting and standing to the night and the day as a figurative rational attribution (isnad majazi 'aqli). Originally, fasting and standing should be attributed to the man, not to the time; this is a case of figurative extension, the relation here being temporal and the indication rational. This is like His saying, the Exalted: "Rather, the scheming of the night and the day." Its origin is: "Rather, your scheming against us during the night and the day," then the verb was attributed to them. His words, ﴿And We will place shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved﴾

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 34, verses 32–33:

The interpretation of the words of God, the Exalted: ﴿Those who were arrogant will say to those who were oppressed, "Was it we who barred you from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you were criminals."﴾ (32)

God, the One who is mentioned, says: ﴿Those who were arrogant﴾ in the world, and became leaders in misguidance and disbelief in God, ﴿to those who were oppressed﴾ in it, who were followers of the people of misguidance among them, when they said to them, ﴿Had it not been for you, we would have been believers﴾: ﴿Was it we who barred you from guidance﴾ and prevented you from following the truth ﴿after it had come to you﴾ from God, making it clear to you? ﴿Rather, you were criminals﴾: it was your preference for disbelief in God over faith that prevented you from following guidance and believing in God and His Messenger.

* *

The interpretation of the words of God, the Exalted: ﴿And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Rather, it was the scheming of the night and the day when you commanded us to disbelieve in God and set up rivals to Him." And they will conceal their regret when they see the punishment. We will place shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾ (33)

God, the One who is mentioned, says: ﴿And those who were oppressed﴾ from among the disbelievers in God in the world, who were followers of their leaders in misguidance, will say ﴿to those who were arrogant﴾ in it, who were their leaders: ﴿Rather, the scheming﴾ of you against us ﴿by the night and the day﴾ diverted us from guidance ﴿when you commanded us to disbelieve in God and set up for Him﴾ equals and likenesses in worship and divinity. The attribution to the night and the day is made, the meaning being what we have mentioned: the scheming of the arrogant against the oppressed during the night and the day. This is in accordance with the breadth of Arab speech in what its meaning is known from their discourse, namely the transfer of the attribute of one thing to another. You say to a man: "O so-and-so, your day is fasting and your night is standing," and as the poet said:

"You slept, while the night of the travelers is not sleeping" [[This is the second half of a verse by Jarir ibn Atiyya al-Khatafi, the Islamic poet, whose first half is: "You have blamed us, O Umm Ghaylan, for travelling by night." (His Diwan, Sawi edition, p. 554). The author cited it to show that you say "O so-and-so, your day is fasting and your night is standing," attributing fasting and standing to the night and the day as a figurative rational attribution (isnad majazi 'aqli). Originally, fasting and standing should be attributed to the man, not to the time; this is a case of figurative extension, the relation here being temporal and the indication rational. This is like His saying, the Exalted: "Rather, the scheming of the night and the day." Its origin is: "Rather, your scheming against us during the night and the day," then the verb was attributed to them. Al-Farra said in (Ma'ani al-Qur'an, folio 274): "His saying, 'Rather, the scheming of the night and the day': scheming does not belong to the night or the day; the meaning is: rather, your scheming by the night and the day. It is also permissible to attribute the verb to the night and the day, them acting as the doers, because the Arabs say: 'your day is fasting, and your night is standing,' then they attribute the verb to the night and the day, and this is the meaning for human beings, as you say: 'your night slept.' End of quote."]]

And the like of that which has already been explained in another place in this book of ours.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 34, verses 35–36:

The interpretation of His statement, exalted is He: ﴿And they said, "We have more wealth and children, and we will not be punished."﴾ ﴿Say, "Indeed, my Lord extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it. But most of the people do not know."﴾

Exalted is He, says: And those who were arrogant toward God from every town to which We sent a warner to Our prophets and messengers said: "We have more wealth and children, and we will not be punished in the Hereafter," because God, if He were not pleased with what we are upon of religion and deeds, would not have granted us wealth and children, nor expanded provision for us. He gave us what He gave us of that only because He was pleased with our deeds, and He preferred us with what He preferred over others for our merit and for our nearness to Him. God says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say to them, O Muhammad: ﴿Indeed, my Lord extends provision﴾ of livelihood and finery in this world ﴿to whom He wills﴾ of His creation ﴿and restricts it﴾, narrowing it for whom He wills, not out of love for those to whom He extends it, nor because of any good in them, nor because of any nearness to Him that they deserve by it, and not out of hatred for those upon whom He restricts it, nor out of disdain. Rather, He does that as a trial and a test for His servants. But most people do not know that God does this as a test for His servants; instead, they think that it is a sign of His love for the one to whom He extends it and of His hatred for the one upon whom He restricts it.

And in accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an, i.e., tafsir) have said.

Mention of those who said this:

He said: This was the statement of the polytheists to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his companions. Those who said so:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿near to Us in position﴾: he said: "nearness."

He, may His praise be exalted, said ﴿bi-allati﴾ (feminine singular) and did not say ﴿bi-allatayn﴾ (dual), though wealth and children are mentioned, and they are two different kinds, because for each kind a plural has been mentioned to which ﴿allati﴾ is suitable. If someone said that he intended by it one of the two kinds, his statement would not be far-fetched, and that is like the saying of the poet:

"We are content with what we have, and you with what you have, and opinions differ."

[The verse is by Qays ibn al-Khatim from a poem in the meter al-munsarih, as cited in Ma'ahid al-Tansis Sharh Shawahid al-Talkhis by 'Abd al-Rahim al-'Abbasi, and its discussion was previously treated at length (10:122), so refer back there.]

He did not say "radiyani" (two who are content).

The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of this. Some of them said: The meaning is: "And it is not your wealth nor your children that bring you near to Us in position, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, for their wealth and children bring them near to God through their obedience to God in regard to them and their fulfilment of His right concerning them, nearness, unlike the people of disbelief in God."

Those who said so:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding God's saying ﴿except for those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: "Their wealth and children did not harm the believers in this world." And he recited ﴿For those who do good is the best reward and more﴾ [10:26]. So "the best reward" is Paradise, and "more" is what God gave them in this world, which He did not hold them accountable for, as He held others accountable. Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 38–39:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Those who strive against Our signs, seeking to frustrate them, they will be brought forth into the punishment﴾ [38] ﴿Say: "Indeed, my Lord extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him. And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it, and He is the best of providers."﴾ [39]

His, the Exalted's, saying means: Those who work against Our signs, meaning Our proofs and the verses of Our Book, seeking to nullify them and wanting to extinguish their light, with helpers, supposing that they can escape Us by themselves and render Us powerless, ﴿they will be brought forth into the punishment﴾, meaning: they will be brought forth to the punishment of Hell on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Say: "Indeed, my Lord extends provision to whom He wills of His servants"﴾. His, the Exalted's, saying means: Say, O Muhammad, indeed my Lord extends provision to whomever He wills of His creation, so He widens it for him as an honour for him and as other than an honour, and He restricts it for whomever He wills among them, so He constricts it for him as a humiliation for him and as other than a humiliation, but rather as a trial and a test. ﴿And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it﴾. It means: and whatever you, O people, spend in obedience to God, God will replace it for you.

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it﴾: He said: "That which is without extravagance and without stinginess."

It means: He is better than whoever is said to provide and is described as such, because it may be said of others than Him: "So-and-so provides for his family and dependents."

His saying, exalted is He, means: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists of your people: I admonish you, O people, with one thing, and it is obedience to Allah.

As related:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿I admonish you with one thing﴾, he said: with the obedience to Allah.

* *

As for His saying ﴿that you stand up before Allah, in pairs and individually﴾:

It means: and that one thing with which I admonish you is that you stand up for Allah in twos and individually. ﴿Furada﴾ [[Perhaps: fardan wa fardan, i.e., that you stand in twos and one by one.]] Here "an" (that) is in a position of genitive, as an explanatory apposition of "the one thing."

The people of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to me, saying: Isa narrated to us, and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿that you stand up before Allah, in pairs and individually﴾, he said: one by one and two by two.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Said narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Say: I admonish you with one thing: that you stand up before Allah, in pairs and individually﴾: man by man and two men.

It has been said: The reason it was said "I admonish you with one thing" is that this one thing is that you stand up for Allah with sincere counsel and with the abandoning of desire. ﴿In pairs﴾ means: a man of you stands with another, and the two of you confer together in debate: Have you ever known Muhammad (ﷺ) to have madness at all? Then each of you stands alone, reflects, and considers individually whether that was in him. Then you will know at that time that he is a warner to you.

As for His saying ﴿Then reflect: there is no madness in your companion﴾:

It means: because he is not a madman.

It means: Muhammad is only a warner to you, warning you of Allah's punishment for your disbelief in Him, before the punishment of Hell, before you enter it. And His saying "he" refers to the name of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 47:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you, it is yours. My reward is only from Allah, and He is Witness over all things.﴾ (34:47)

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Say, O Muhammad, to your people who deny you and reject what you have brought them from your Lord: I have not asked of you any payment (ju'l) in exchange for warning you of the punishment of Allah and frightening you with His might, nor for my counsel to you in my command that you believe in Allah and act in obedience to Him; and it is yours, for I have no need of it. The meaning of the speech is: Say to them: I have not asked you for any payment for that, so that you would accuse me and think that I only called you to follow me in order to take wealth from you.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you﴾, i.e., payment (ju'l), ﴿it is yours﴾, he said: I have not asked you for a payment for Islam.

* *

As for His saying ﴿My reward is only from Allah﴾:

It means: My reward for calling you to belief in Allah and acting in obedience to Him, and conveying His message to you, is only from Allah. ﴿And He is Witness over all things﴾ means: Allah is a witness to the truth of what I say to you, bearing witness for me to it, and to everything else besides.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Indeed, my Lord casts down the truth; He is the Knower of the unseen."﴾ (34:48) ﴿Say, "The truth has come, and falsehood can neither originate anything nor restore it."﴾ (34:49)

His Majesty, may His praise be exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people: ﴿Indeed, my Lord casts down with the truth﴾, which is the revelation; meaning, He sends it down from the heaven, and casts it to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿He is the Knower of the unseen﴾, meaning: the Knower of what is hidden from sight and has no visible manifestation, and of what has not yet come into being among what will exist. This is an attribute of the Lord, but it has been put in the nominative (raf') because it comes after the predicate (khabar), and this is how the Arabs do it when an epithet (na't) follows the predicate: they make the epithet follow the case-ending (i'rab) of what precedes it in the predicate. So they say: "Inna abaka yaqumu al-karimu" (Indeed your father stands, the noble one), where al-karim is put in the nominative according to what you have described; the accusative is also permissible, since it is an epithet of "the father," and so it follows his case.

The "falsehood," as the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have explained, is Iblis. ﴿Nor can it restore it﴾, meaning: nor can it bring it back to life after its annihilation.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 34, verse 51:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And if you could see when they are terrified, but there will be no escape, and they will be seized from a near place﴾

His saying, exalted is His remembrance, to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): And if you could see, O Muhammad, when they are terrified.

The scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding who is meant by this verse. Some of them said: It refers to those polytheists whom He described with His saying, ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them, they say, "This is not but a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers used to worship"﴾. He said: And by His saying ﴿when they are terrified, but there will be no escape, and they will be seized from a near place﴾ is meant the moment the vengeance of God descends upon them in this world.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿And if you could see when they are terrified ...﴾ to the end of the verse, he said: This is from the punishment of this world.

I was told on the authority of al-Husayn, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His saying ﴿and they will be seized from a near place﴾, he said: This is the punishment of this world.

Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And if you could see when they are terrified, but there will be no escape ...﴾ to the end of the surah, he said: These are the slain of the polytheists from the people of Badr; this verse was revealed concerning them. He said: They are those who exchanged the favour of God for disbelief and caused their people to alight in the abode of destruction, Hell, the polytheists of Badr.

Others said: By this is meant an army that will be swallowed up by the earth in a desert (bayda').

Mention of those who said this:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Sa'id, regarding His saying ﴿And if you could see when they are terrified, but there will be no escape﴾, he said: They are the army that will be swallowed up in the desert; one man from among them will remain to inform people of what befell his companions.

'Isam ibn Rawwad ibn al-Jarrah narrated to us, he said: my father narrated to us, he said: Sufyan ibn Sa'id narrated to us, he said: Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir narrated to me, from Ribi' ibn Hirash, he said: I heard Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman say: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said, and he mentioned a trial that will occur between the people of the east and the west, he said: While they are in that state, al-Sufyani will come out upon them from the dry valley at the height of that turmoil, until he descends upon Damascus, and he will send two armies: an army to the east and an army to Medina. They will alight in the land of Babylon, in the cursed city and the wicked land, and they will kill more than three thousand there, and they will rip open the bellies of more than a hundred women there, and they will kill there three hundred men of the Banu al-'Abbas. Then they will go down to Kufa and ruin what is around it. Then they will come out heading for Syria, and the banner of this one will come out from Kufa, and it will overtake that army from it on the two groups, and they will kill them, and not one informer will escape from them, and they will rescue what is in their hands of captives and spoils. And his following army will leave Medina, and they will plunder it for three days and nights. Then they will come out heading for Mecca, and when they are in the desert, God will send Gabriel, and he will say: O Gabriel, go and annihilate them. He will strike it with his foot, a strike by which God will swallow them up. That is His saying in Surah Saba': ﴿And if you could see when they are terrified, but there will be no escape ...﴾ the verse. Not one of them will escape except two men, one a bearer of good news and the other a warner, and they are from Juhayna. Hence the saying came:
